title.zh: 卷一百五十三 列傳第七十八 段秀實 顏真卿
title.en: Volume 153 Biographies 78: Duan Xiushi, Yan Zhenqing
title.raw: 卷一百五十三 列傳第七十八 段秀實 顏真卿 Volume 153 Biographies 78: Duan Xiushi, Yan Zhenqing

sentences.zh: 段秀實，字成公，本姑臧人。

translations.literal: Duan Xiushi, styled Chenggong, was originally a native of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi, whose courtesy name was Chenggong, came from Guzang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖師濬，仕為隴州刺史，留不歸，更為汧陽人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shi Jun served as prefect of Long Prefecture, remained and did not return, and became a man of Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shi Jun had served as prefect of Long Prefecture; he stayed in the region rather than return home, and the family thereafter counted as natives of Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 秀實六歲，母疾病，不勺飲至七日，病間乃肯食，時號「孝童」。

translations.literal: When Xiushi was six, his mother fell ill; he refused even a spoonful of drink for seven days, and only when her illness eased would he eat; at the time he was called the "Filial Boy."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiushi was six, his mother fell gravely ill. For seven days he would not take so much as a spoonful of food or drink, and ate only after her condition improved. People called him the "Filial Boy."

sentences.zh: 及長，沈厚能斷，慨然有濟世意。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was deep and steady and able to decide matters; he was filled with resolve to aid the world.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured, he proved grave, steadfast, and decisive, with a fervent desire to serve the common good.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，其友易之，秀實曰：「搜章擿句，不足以立功。」

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination; a friend urged him to change [course]. Xiushi said, "Searching out passages and plucking out phrases is not enough to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination, but a friend urged him to change course. Xiushi said, "Picking through texts for quotations will never win real achievement.

sentences.zh: 乃棄去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He left the scholarly path behind.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，從安西節度使馬靈詧討護密有功，授安西府別將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, he followed the Anxi military commissioner Ma Lingzhao in campaigning against Humi with merit, and was appointed deputy general of the Anxi headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 4 (745), he followed Anxi military commissioner Ma Lingzhao on a successful campaign against Humi and was appointed deputy general of the Anxi headquarters.

sentences.zh: 靈詧罷，又事高仙芝。

translations.literal: When Lingzhao was dismissed, he next served Gao Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingzhao left office, he entered the service of Gao Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 仙芝討大食，圍怛邏斯城。

translations.literal: Xianzhi campaigned against Dashi and besieged the city of Talas.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi marched against the Arabs and laid siege to Talas.

sentences.zh: 會虜救至，仙芝兵卻，士相失。

translations.literal: Just then the enemy's relief force arrived; Xianzhi's army withdrew, and the soldiers lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy reinforcements arrived, Xianzhi pulled his army back in disorder, and the troops were scattered.

sentences.zh: 秀實夜聞副將李嗣業聲，識之，因責曰：「憚敵而奔，非勇也；

translations.literal: At night Xiushi heard the voice of the deputy general Li Siye, recognized him, and rebuked him, saying, "To flee for fear of the enemy is not courage;
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiushi heard the voice of deputy general Li Siye, recognized him, and rebuked him: "Running from the enemy out of fear is not courage;

sentences.zh: 免己陷眾，非仁也。」

translations.literal: to save oneself and abandon the multitude is not humanity.
translations.idiomatic: saving yourself while leaving the rest to perish is not humanity.

sentences.zh: 嗣業慚，乃與秀實收散卒，復成軍，還安西，請秀實為判官。

translations.literal: Siye was ashamed; he then joined Xiushi in gathering the scattered soldiers, re-formed the army, returned to Anxi, and requested Xiushi as his staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Siye joined Xiushi in rallying the scattered troops, re-formed the army, and returned to Anxi, where he asked that Xiushi serve as his staff judge.

sentences.zh: 遷隴州大推府果毅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be guoyi of the Great Tui Office of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to guoyi of the Great Tui Office in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後從封常清討大勃律，次賀薩勞城，與虜戰，勝之。

translations.literal: Later he followed Feng Changqing in campaigning against Greater Bolü, halted at Hesalao City, fought the barbarians, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Feng Changqing against Greater Bolü, encamped at Hesalao City, fought the enemy, and won.

sentences.zh: 常清逐北，秀實曰：「賊出羸師，餌我也，請大索。」

translations.literal: Changqing pursued north; Xiushi said, "The enemy has sent out a weak force to bait us—I ask for a thorough search.
translations.idiomatic: As Changqing pressed the pursuit northward, Xiushi said, "They have put out a weak detachment to lure us on. I ask that we search the area thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 悉得其廋伏，虜師唧。

translations.literal: They found all their hidden ambushes; the barbarian army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: They uncovered every hidden ambush, and the enemy army was put to rout.

sentences.zh: 改綏德府折沖都尉。

translations.literal: He was changed to be zhechong commandant of Suide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed zhechong commandant of Suide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在靈武，詔嗣業以安西兵五千走行在。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, he ordered Siye to hurry to the imperial camp with five thousand Anxi troops.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, he ordered Siye to march five thousand Anxi troops posthaste to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 節度使梁宰欲逗留觀變，嗣業陰然可。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Liang Zai wished to linger and watch how events developed; Siye secretly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner Liang Zai wanted to delay departure and watch how events unfolded, and Siye quietly agreed.

sentences.zh: 秀實責謂曰：「天子方急，臣下乃欲晏然，公常自稱大丈夫，今誠兒女耳。」

translations.literal: Xiushi rebuked him, saying, "The Son of Heaven is in urgent straits, yet his subjects wish to sit at ease—you often call yourself a great man, but now you are truly no more than a woman or child.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi rebuked him: "The Son of Heaven is in desperate straits, and you would sit idle? You call yourself a great man—today you act like a timid child.

sentences.zh: 嗣業因固請宰，遂東師，以秀實為副。

translations.literal: Siye thereupon pressed Zai firmly, and they then marched east; Xiushi served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Siye pressed Zai until he yielded, and the army marched east with Xiushi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 嗣業為節度使，而秀實方居父喪，表起為義王友，充節度判官。

translations.literal: When Siye became military commissioner, Xiushi was in mourning for his father; he was summoned by memorial to be Friend of the Prince of Yi and served as the commissioner's staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Siye became military commissioner, Xiushi was still in mourning for his father; summoned from mourning, he was named Friend of the Prince of Yi and served as the commissioner's staff judge.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒奔鄴，嗣業與諸將圍之，以輜重委河內，署秀實兼懷州長史，知州事，兼留後。

translations.literal: An Qingxu fled to Ye; Siye and the generals besieged him, entrusted the baggage train to Henei, and appointed Xiushi concurrently as chief administrator of Huai Prefecture, in charge of prefectural affairs and also as acting rear commander.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu fled to Ye, Siye and the other generals besieged him, left the baggage train at Henei, and appointed Xiushi concurrently chief administrator of Huai Prefecture, with charge of prefectural affairs and acting rear commander.

sentences.zh: 時師老財覂，秀實督饋系道，募士市馬以助軍。

translations.literal: At the time the army was weary and funds were exhausted; Xiushi supervised supplies along the route, recruited men, and purchased horses to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army was exhausted and funds were running out; Xiushi supervised supply lines, recruited troops, and bought horses to keep the campaign going.

sentences.zh: 諸軍戰愁思岡，嗣業中流矢卒，眾推荔非元禮代將其軍。

translations.literal: The armies fought at Chousigang; Siye was struck by a stray arrow and died; the troops chose Lifei Yuanli to take command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Chousigang, Siye was killed by a stray arrow, and the troops chose Lifei Yuanli to replace him.

sentences.zh: 秀實聞之，即遺白孝德書，使發卒護喪送河內，親與將吏迎諸境，傾私財葬之。

translations.literal: When Xiushi heard of it, he immediately sent a letter to Bai Xiaode asking him to dispatch troops to escort the coffin to Henei; he personally went with officers to meet them at the border and spent his private wealth on the burial.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news, Xiushi at once wrote to Bai Xiaode asking him to send troops to escort the coffin to Henei; he met the procession at the border with his officers and paid for the burial out of his own purse.

sentences.zh: 元禮高其義，奏擢試光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Yuanli admired his righteousness and memorialized that he be promoted on probation to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli admired his conduct and memorialized that he be promoted on probation to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 俄而元禮為麾下所殺，將佐多死，惟秀實以恩信為士卒所服，皆羅拜不敢害，更推白孝德為節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanli was killed by his subordinates; many staff officers died, but only Xiushi, because the soldiers trusted him through grace and faith, were all made to bow in ranks and dared not harm him; they instead chose Bai Xiaode as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuanli was killed by his own troops and many officers perished with him, but the soldiers trusted Xiushi and would not harm him; they lined up to pay him homage and instead chose Bai Xiaode as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秀實凡佐三府，益知名。

translations.literal: Xiushi had in all assisted three headquarters and became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Having served three military headquarters in succession, Xiushi grew still more famous.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃襲京師，代宗幸陝，勸孝德即日鼓行入援。

translations.literal: At the time the Tibetans raided the capital; Emperor Daizong went to Shaan; he urged Xiaode to beat the drums that very day and march in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the capital and Emperor Daizong withdrew to Shaan, Xiushi urged Xiaode to march to the rescue without delay.

sentences.zh: 孝德徙邠甯，署支度營田副使。

translations.literal: Xiaode was transferred to Binning and appointed deputy commissioner for logistics and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaode was transferred to Binning, Xiushi was appointed deputy commissioner for logistics and military colonies.

sentences.zh: 於是邠寧乏食，乃請屯奉天，仰給畿內。

translations.literal: Thereupon Binning lacked food, so he requested to encamp at Fengtian and rely on supplies from within the metropolitan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: With Binning short of grain, he asked to encamp at Fengtian and draw supplies from the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時公廩竭，縣吏不知所出，皆逃去，軍輒散剽，孝德不能制。

translations.literal: At the time the public granaries were exhausted; county clerks did not know what to do and all fled; the army constantly scattered to plunder, and Xiaode could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Public granaries were empty, county clerks fled in confusion, and troops scattered to plunder at will—Xiaode could not control them.

sentences.zh: 秀實曰：「使我為軍候，豈至是邪？」

translations.literal: Xiushi said, "If you put me in charge as army overseer, would it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi said, "Put me in charge as army overseer, and it would never come to this.

sentences.zh: 司馬王稷言之，遂知奉天行營事。

translations.literal: The staff officer Wang Ji spoke of it, and he was then put in charge of affairs at the Fengtian field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Wang Ji relayed the offer, and Xiushi was put in charge of the Fengtian field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 號令嚴壹，軍中畏戢。

translations.literal: His orders were strict and uniform; within the army all feared and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were strict and uniform, and discipline returned to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 兵還，孝德薦為涇州刺史，封張掖郡王。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Xiaode recommended him as prefect of Jing Prefecture and enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhangye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, Xiaode recommended him as prefect of Jing and had him enfeoffed as Prince of Zhangye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時郭子儀為副元帥，居蒲，子晞以檢校尚書領行營節度使，屯邠州。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Ziyi was deputy supreme commander, residing at Pu; his son Xi, holding the acting title of Minister, led the field headquarters as military commissioner and was encamped at Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was then deputy supreme commander at Pu; his son Xi, with the acting title of Minister, held field headquarters command and was encamped at Bin.

sentences.zh: 士放縱不法，邠人之嗜惡者，納賄竄名伍中，因肆志，吏不得問。

translations.literal: The soldiers were unrestrained and lawless; vicious men of Bin bribed their way into the ranks and thus indulged their will; officials could not inquire into them.
translations.idiomatic: His troops ran wild. Villains of Bin bribed their way into the ranks and did as they pleased, beyond any official's reach.

sentences.zh: 白晝群行丐頡於市，有不嗛，輒擊傷市人，椎釜鬲甕盎盈道，至撞害孕婦。

translations.literal: By day they went in groups begging and extorting in the market; if anyone was not satisfied, they would beat and injure townspeople; they smashed pots, tripods, jars, and bowls until the roads were full, even striking and killing pregnant women.
translations.idiomatic: By day they roamed the markets in gangs, extorting goods; anyone who refused was beaten. They smashed cookware until the streets were littered with debris, and even killed pregnant women.

sentences.zh: 孝德不敢劾，秀實自州以狀白府，願計事，至則曰：「天子以生人付公治，公見人被暴害，恬然，且大亂，若何？」

translations.literal: Xiaode dared not impeach them; Xiushi from his prefecture sent a report to the headquarters, asking to discuss affairs; when he arrived he said, "The Son of Heaven has entrusted the living people to you for governance—you see men suffering violence and remain at ease; soon there will be great disorder—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode dared not act. Xiushi reported from his prefecture to headquarters and asked to discuss the crisis. When he arrived he said, "The Son of Heaven entrusted these people to your care. You watch them suffer violence and do nothing—how long before total chaos?

sentences.zh: 孝德曰：「願奉教。」

translations.literal: Xiaode said, "I am willing to follow your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode said, "I will follow your guidance."

sentences.zh: 因請曰：「秀實不忍人無寇暴死，亂天子邊事。

translations.literal: He then requested, saying, "Xiushi cannot bear that people should die violently though there is no enemy, throwing the Son of Heaven's frontier affairs into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi went on: "I cannot stand by while innocents are killed in peacetime and the frontier is thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 公誠以為都虞候，能為公已亂。」

translations.literal: If you truly appoint me as chief military police officer, I can end the disorder for you."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint me chief military police officer, and I will end this disorder for you."

sentences.zh: 孝德即檄署付軍。

translations.literal: Xiaode immediately issued an order appointing him and handed him over to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode issued the appointment at once and turned him over to the army.

sentences.zh: 俄而晞士十七人入市取酒，刺酒翁，壞釀器，秀實列卒取之，斷首置槊上，植市門外。

translations.literal: Before long seventeen of Xi's soldiers entered the market to get wine, stabbed the wine seller, and broke the brewing vessels; Xiushi lined up troops, seized them, cut off their heads, placed them on spears, and planted them outside the market gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon seventeen of Xi's men went into the market for wine, stabbed the wine seller, and smashed his equipment. Xiushi seized them, beheaded them, and planted their heads on spears outside the market gate.

sentences.zh: 一營大噪，盡甲，孝德恐，召秀實曰：「奈何？」

translations.literal: One entire camp roared in uproar and all donned armor; Xiaode was afraid and summoned Xiushi, saying, "What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The whole camp erupted in uproar and armed for battle. Terrified, Xiaode summoned Xiushi: "What now?

sentences.zh: 秀實曰：「請辭於軍。」

translations.literal: Xiushi said, "Allow me to explain to the army."
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi said, "Let me speak to them."

sentences.zh: 乃解佩刀，選老鐍一人持馬，至晞門下。

translations.literal: He then unbuckled his belt sword, chose one old veteran to hold his horse, and went to Xi's gate.
translations.idiomatic: He unbuckled his sword, chose one old veteran to hold his horse, and went alone to Xi's gate.

sentences.zh: 甲者出，秀實笑且入，曰：「殺一老卒，何甲也！

translations.literal: Armored men came out; Xiushi smiled as he entered and said, "For killing one old soldier, why don armor!
translations.idiomatic: Armored men rushed out. Xiushi smiled as he entered and said, "All this armor over one old soldier killed—why?

sentences.zh: 吾戴頭來矣。」

translations.literal: I have come wearing my head.
translations.idiomatic: I have come offering my own head.

sentences.zh: 甲為愕眙。

translations.literal: The armored men were struck dumb with astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers stood stunned.

sentences.zh: 因曉之曰：「尚書固負若屬邪，副元帥固負若屬邪？

translations.literal: He then enlightened them, saying, "Has the Minister truly wronged you? Has the deputy supreme commander truly wronged you?
translations.idiomatic: He reasoned with them: "Has the Minister wronged you? Has the deputy supreme commander wronged you?

sentences.zh: 奈何欲以亂敗郭氏！」

translations.literal: Why would you wish to ruin the Guo family through disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Why would you destroy the Guo family through mutiny?

sentences.zh: 晞出，秀實曰：「副元帥功塞天地，當務始終。

translations.literal: Xi came out; Xiushi said, "The deputy supreme commander's merit fills heaven and earth—he should attend to the beginning and the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi came out, Xiushi said, "Your father's merit fills heaven and earth. He must see matters through to the end.

sentences.zh: 今尚書恣卒為暴，使亂天子邊，欲誰歸罪？

translations.literal: Now the Minister indulges his soldiers in violence, throwing the Son of Heaven's frontier into disorder—upon whom do you wish guilt to fall?
translations.idiomatic: You let your men run wild and throw the frontier into chaos—who will bear the blame?

sentences.zh: 罪且及副元帥。

translations.literal: The guilt will reach the deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The guilt will reach your father.

sentences.zh: 今邠惡子弟以貨竄名軍籍中，殺害人，藉藉如是，幾日不大亂？

translations.literal: Now vicious youths of Bin bribe their way into the army rolls and kill people—so widespread is it—how many days before great disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Vicious youths of Bin buy their way into your rolls and murder at will. How long before total chaos?

sentences.zh: 亂由尚書出。

translations.literal: Disorder will issue from the Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The disorder will start with you.

sentences.zh: 人皆曰：尚書以副元帥故不戢士。

translations.literal: Everyone says: the Minister does not restrain his soldiers because of the deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone will say the Minister failed to restrain his men because of his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 然則郭氏功名，其與存者有幾！」

translations.literal: Then of the Guo family's fame and merit, how much will remain!"
translations.idiomatic: How much of the Guo family's fame and fortune will survive?"

sentences.zh: 晞再拜曰：「公幸教，晞願奉軍以從。」

translations.literal: Xi bowed twice and said, "Sir, I am fortunate in your instruction; Xi is willing to lead the army in obedience."
translations.idiomatic: Xi bowed twice and said, "Thank you for your guidance. I will bring the army to heel."

sentences.zh: 即叱左右皆解甲，令曰：「敢喧者死！」

translations.literal: He immediately shouted at those on his left and right to all remove their armor, and ordered, "Whoever dares make an uproar dies!"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to remove their armor at once and declared, "Anyone who makes another uproar dies!"

sentences.zh: 秀實曰：「吾未晡食，請設具。」

translations.literal: Xiushi said, "I have not eaten since mid-afternoon—please set out a meal."
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi said, "I have not eaten since mid-afternoon. Please set out a meal."

sentences.zh: 已食，曰：「吾疾作，願宿門下。」

translations.literal: After he had eaten, he said, "My illness is acting up; I wish to lodge at your gate."
translations.idiomatic: After eating he said, "I feel ill and would like to stay the night at your gate."

sentences.zh: 遂臥軍中。

translations.literal: He then lay down within the army camp.
translations.idiomatic: He lay down inside the camp.

sentences.zh: 晞大駭，戒候卒擊柝衛之。

translations.literal: Xi was greatly alarmed and ordered the watch soldiers to strike the clapper and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was terrified and ordered the watch to strike the night clapper and guard him through the night.

sentences.zh: 旦，與俱至孝德所，謝不能。

translations.literal: At dawn he went with him together to Xiaode's place and apologized for his inability [to control the troops].
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they went together to Xiaode's headquarters, where Xi apologized for his failure to control the troops.

sentences.zh: 邠由是安。

translations.literal: Bin was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was pacified from that day on.

sentences.zh: 初，秀實為營田官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiushi was military colony officer,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as military colony officer,

sentences.zh: 涇大將焦令諶取人田自占，給與農，約熟歸其半。

translations.literal: the great general of Jing Jiao Lingchen seized people's fields for himself, supplied them to farmers, and agreed that at harvest half would return to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's senior general Jiao Lingchen had seized private fields, leased them to farmers, and demanded half the harvest.

sentences.zh: 是歲大旱，農告無入，令諶曰：「我知入，不知旱也。」

translations.literal: That year there was great drought; the farmers reported they had no yield. Lingchen said, "I know yield—I do not know drought.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe drought. When farmers reported no yield, Lingchen said, "I deal in harvests, not droughts.

sentences.zh: 責之急，農無以償，往訴秀實。

translations.literal: He pressed them urgently for payment; the farmers had no means to repay and went to appeal to Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed them hard for payment. Unable to pay, they appealed to Xiushi.

sentences.zh: 秀實署牒免之，因使人遜諭令諶。

translations.literal: Xiushi issued a document exempting them and sent someone with courteous words to advise Lingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi issued a document exempting them and sent a courteous message to Lingchen.

sentences.zh: 令諶怒，召農責曰：「我畏段秀實邪？」

translations.literal: Lingchen was angry, summoned the farmers, and rebuked them, saying, "Do I fear Duan Xiushi?
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lingchen summoned the farmers and demanded, "Do I fear Duan Xiushi?

sentences.zh: 以牒置背上，大杖擊二十，輿致廷中。

translations.literal: He placed the document on their backs, beat them heavily with the staff twenty times, and had them carried in a litter to the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He pinned the document to their backs, gave each twenty heavy strokes of the staff, and had them carried into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 秀實泣曰：「乃我困汝。」

translations.literal: Xiushi wept and said, "It was I who brought trouble upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi wept and said, "I am the one who brought this on you.

sentences.zh: 即自裂裳裹瘡注藥，賣己馬以代償。

translations.literal: He immediately tore his own robe to wrap their wounds and apply medicine, and sold his own horse to pay on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: He tore his own robe to dress their wounds, applied medicine, and sold his horse to pay their debt.

sentences.zh: 淮西將尹少榮頗剛鯁，入罵令諶曰：「汝誠人乎！

translations.literal: The Huaixi general Yin Shaorong was quite stern and upright; he went in and cursed Lingchen, saying, "Are you truly a human being!
translations.idiomatic: Huaixi officer Yin Shaorong, a man of fierce integrity, went in and cursed Lingchen: "Are you even human?

sentences.zh: 涇州野如赭，人饑死，而爾必得穀，擊無罪者。

translations.literal: The fields of Jing Prefecture are red as ochre, people starve to death, yet you insist on getting grain and beat the guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: The fields of Jing are bare as ochre, people are starving to death, yet you demand grain and beat the innocent.

sentences.zh: 段公，仁信大人，惟一馬，賣而市穀入汝，汝取之不恥？

translations.literal: Lord Duan, a man of humanity and faith, had only one horse—he sold it to buy grain and give it to you—are you not ashamed to take it?
translations.idiomatic: Lord Duan, a man of humanity and trust, had only one horse. He sold it to buy grain for you. Are you not ashamed to take it?

sentences.zh: 凡為人傲天災、犯大人、擊無罪者，尚不愧奴隸邪！」

translations.literal: For anyone who defies heaven's calamity, offends a great man, and strikes the guiltless—would he not even be ashamed before a slave!
translations.idiomatic: A man who defies heaven's calamity, insults his betters, and beats the innocent—would he not blush before a slave?

sentences.zh: 令諶聞，大愧流汗，曰：「吾終不可以見段公。」

translations.literal: When Lingchen heard it, he was greatly ashamed and sweat streamed down; he said, "I can never again face Lord Duan."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Lingchen flushed with shame and sweat and said, "I can never face Lord Duan again."

sentences.zh: 一夕，自恨死。

translations.literal: In one night he died of self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died of remorse.

sentences.zh: 馬璘代孝德，每所咨逮。

translations.literal: When Ma Lin replaced Xiaode, on every matter he consulted Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Lin replaced Xiaode, he consulted Xiushi on every matter.

sentences.zh: 璘處決不當，固爭之，不從不止。

translations.literal: When Lin's decisions were improper, Xiushi firmly disputed them and would not stop until Lin yielded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin's decisions were wrong, Xiushi argued firmly and would not relent until Lin yielded.

sentences.zh: 始，璘城涇州，秀實為留後，以勞加御史中丞。

translations.literal: At first, when Lin fortified Jing Prefecture, Xiushi was acting rear commander; for his labors he was additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin first fortified Jing, Xiushi served as acting rear commander and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief for his labors.

sentences.zh: 大曆三年，遂徙涇州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, the army was then transferred to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 3 (768), the army was transferred to Jing.

sentences.zh: 是軍自四鎮、北庭赴難，征伐數有功，既驟徙，相與出怨言。

translations.literal: This army had come from the Four Garrisons and Beiting to answer the crisis; in campaigns they had achieved merit many times; after being suddenly transferred, they together voiced complaints.
translations.idiomatic: These troops had marched from the Four Garrisons and Beiting to save the dynasty and had won many victories; the sudden transfer stirred widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 別將王童之謀作亂，約曰：「聞警鼓而縱。」

translations.literal: The deputy general Wang Tongzhi plotted rebellion and agreed, "When you hear the alarm drum, let loose.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy general Wang Tongzhi plotted mutiny, agreeing that when the alarm drum sounded they would rise.

sentences.zh: 秀實知之，召鼓人，陽怒失節，戒曰：「每籌盡當報。」

translations.literal: Xiushi learned of it, summoned the drummer, feigned anger at his lapse, and warned, "Each time the watch is fully counted you must report."
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi learned of the plot, summoned the drummer, feigned anger at a lapse, and warned, "Report each time the watch is fully counted."

sentences.zh: 因延數刻，盡四鼓而曙。

translations.literal: He thereby delayed several quarters; all four watches of the night had sounded before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He delayed the watches by several quarters until all four night watches had sounded before dawn.

sentences.zh: 明日，復有告者曰：「夜焚稿積，約救火則亂。」

translations.literal: The next day there was again an informant who said, "Tonight they will burn the hay stores; they have agreed that at fire-fighting they will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The next day another informant said, "Tonight they will burn the hay stores and use the fire drill as cover for mutiny.

sentences.zh: 秀實嚴警備。

translations.literal: Xiushi tightened the guard and preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi tightened security.

sentences.zh: 夜中果火發，令軍中曰：「敢救者斬！」

translations.literal: In the middle of the night fire indeed broke out; he ordered the army, "Whoever dares to rescue dies!
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the night as predicted. He ordered the army, "Anyone who tries to fight the fire will be executed!

sentences.zh: 童之居外，請入，不許。

translations.literal: Tongzhi was outside and asked to enter; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi, who was outside the camp, asked to enter and was refused.

sentences.zh: 明日，捕之，並其黨八人斬以徇，曰：「後徙者族！」

translations.literal: The next day he arrested him, and together with eight of his faction beheaded them as a warning, saying, "Whoever mutinies later—his clan!
translations.idiomatic: The next day he arrested Tongzhi and beheaded him with eight accomplices as a warning: "Anyone who mutinies again—his whole clan!

sentences.zh: 軍遂遷涇州。

translations.literal: The army then moved to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The army then completed its transfer to Jing.

sentences.zh: 于時，食無久儲，郛無居人，朝廷患之，詔璘領鄭、潁二州以佐軍，命秀實為留後。

translations.literal: At that time there was no long-term store of food, and the outer walls had no inhabitants; the court was troubled by this and ordered Lin to take charge of Zheng and Ying prefectures to aid the army, appointing Xiushi as acting rear commander.
translations.idiomatic: Food stores were depleted and the city walls stood empty; the court was alarmed. Lin was ordered to draw supplies from Zheng and Ying to support the army, with Xiushi as acting rear commander.

sentences.zh: 軍不乏資，二州以治。

translations.literal: The army lacked no supplies; the two prefectures were thereby well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The army never wanted for supplies, and the two prefectures prospered.

sentences.zh: 璘嘉其績，奏為行軍司馬，兼都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Lin praised his achievements and memorialized that he be made campaigning staff marshal, concurrently overall commander of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Lin praised his achievements and had him appointed campaigning staff marshal and overall commander of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇邊，戰鹽倉，師不利。

translations.literal: The Tibetans raided the frontier; they fought at Yancang; the army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the frontier, the army fought at Yancang and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 璘為虜隔，未能還，都將引潰兵先入，秀實讓曰：「兵法：失將，麾下斬。

translations.literal: Lin was cut off by the barbarians and could not return; the commanders led the routed troops in first; Xiushi reproached them, saying, "By the art of war: when the general is lost, subordinates are beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was cut off by the enemy and could not return. Commanders led the routed troops into camp ahead of him. Xiushi rebuked them: "By the art of war, when the general is lost, his subordinates are beheaded.

sentences.zh: 公等忘死，而欲安其家邪！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen forget death yet wish to secure your households!
translations.idiomatic: You forget your duty to die with your commander, yet you wish to go home to your families?

sentences.zh: 乃悉城中士，使銳將統之，依東原列奇兵，示賊將戰。

translations.literal: He then gathered all soldiers in the city, had sharp generals command them, arrayed elite troops along the eastern plain, and showed the enemy that he would fight.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered every soldier in the city, placed crack officers in command, deployed elite troops on the eastern plain, and made a show of readiness to give battle.

sentences.zh: 虜望之，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The barbarians saw this and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw this and dared not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 俄而璘得歸。

translations.literal: Before long Lin was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lin made his way back.

sentences.zh: 久之，璘有疾，請秀實攝節度副使。

translations.literal: After a long while Lin fell ill and requested that Xiushi act as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin fell ill, he asked Xiushi to serve as acting deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秀實按甲備變，璘卒，命願將馬頔主喪，李漢惠主賓客，家人位於堂，宗族位於廷，賓將位於牙內，尉吏士卒位於營次，非其親，不得居喪側。

translations.literal: Xiushi kept armor ready against disturbance; when Lin died, he ordered Colonel Ma Di to preside over the mourning, Li Hanhui to receive guests; family members were placed in the hall, clansmen in the courtyard, guest officers inside the headquarters gate, clerks and soldiers at the camp stations—those not kin might not stand beside the bier.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi kept the army on alert. When Lin died, he put Colonel Ma Di in charge of the funeral and Li Hanhui in charge of receiving guests. He assigned places for family in the hall, clansmen in the courtyard, guest officers inside headquarters, and clerks and soldiers at camp—only kin might stand beside the bier.

sentences.zh: 朝夕臨，三日止。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he attended; on the third day he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He attended morning and evening for three days, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 有族談離立者，皆捕囚之。

translations.literal: Any clansmen who stood apart talking were all seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone among the clan who stood apart whispering was seized and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 都虞候史廷幹、裨將崔珍、張景華欲謀亂，秀實送廷幹京師，徙珍、景華於外，一軍遂安。

translations.literal: Chief military police officer Shi Tinggan and staff generals Cui Zhen and Zhang Jinghua wished to plot rebellion; Xiushi sent Tinggan to the capital, transferred Zhen and Jinghua elsewhere, and the whole army was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chief military police officer Shi Tinggan and staff generals Cui Zhen and Zhang Jinghua plotted mutiny. Xiushi sent Tinggan to the capital and transferred Zhen and Jinghua elsewhere, and the army was pacified.

sentences.zh: 即拜四鎮北庭行軍、涇原鄭潁節度使。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed campaigning commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting, and military commissioner of Jingyuan, Zheng, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed campaigning commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting and military commissioner of Jingyuan, Zheng, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 數年，吐蕃不敢犯塞。

translations.literal: For several years the Tibetans did not dare violate the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: For several years the Tibetans dared not raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又按格令，官使二料取其一，非公會不舉樂飲酒；

translations.literal: He also enforced regulations: official envoys took one of two stipends; unless it was a public gathering he did not have music played or wine drunk;
translations.idiomatic: He enforced regulations strictly: envoys received only half their usual stipends; he allowed music and wine only at official gatherings;

sentences.zh: 室無妓媵，無贏財；

translations.literal: his quarters had no singing girls or concubines, and no surplus wealth;
translations.idiomatic: his quarters held no singing girls or concubines, and he accumulated no private wealth;

sentences.zh: 賓佐至，議軍政，不及私。

translations.literal: when guests and aides came, they discussed military and civil affairs and did not touch on private matters.
translations.idiomatic: when guests and aides visited, they discussed military affairs only, never private matters.

sentences.zh: 十三年來朝，對蓬萊殿，代宗問所以安邊者，畫地以對，件別條陳。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he came to court, was received at Penglai Hall; Emperor Daizong asked how to secure the frontier; he drew on the ground to answer and set forth each item separately.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he came to court and was received at Penglai Hall. When Emperor Daizong asked how to secure the frontier, he traced a map on the ground and laid out his plan item by item.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，慰賚良渥，又賜第一區，實封百戶。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, comforted and rewarded him generously, and also granted him one top-ranked residence and a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, rewarded him generously, granted him a top-ranked residence, and gave him a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 還之鎮。

translations.literal: He returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was additionally made Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建中初，宰相楊炎追元載議，欲城原州，詔中使問狀，秀實言：「方春不可興土功，請須農隙。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Chancellor Yang Yan pursued Yuan Zai's proposal and wished to fortify Yuan Prefecture; an imperial envoy was ordered to inquire into the matter; Xiushi said, "In spring one cannot undertake earthworks—please wait until the farming interval.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era, Chancellor Yang Yan revived Yuan Zai's plan to fortify Yuan Prefecture. When an imperial envoy came to inquire, Xiushi said, "Earthworks cannot begin in spring. Wait until the farming season ends.

sentences.zh: 炎謂沮己，遂召為司農卿。

translations.literal: Yan considered this obstruction of himself and thereupon summoned him to be Director of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yan took this as obstruction and summoned him to the capital as Director of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 硃泚反，以秀實失兵，必恨憤，且素有人望，使騎往迎。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, because Xiushi had lost his army he would surely harbor resentment, and moreover he had long enjoyed public esteem—he sent horsemen to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he reckoned that Xiushi, having lost his command, must be bitter, and that his long-standing reputation made him worth winning over. He sent horsemen to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 秀實與子弟訣而入，泚喜曰：「公來，吾事成矣。」

translations.literal: Xiushi took leave of his sons and younger brothers and entered; Ci was pleased and said, "Sir, you have come—my affair is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi bade farewell to his sons and brothers and entered. Ci was delighted: "With you here, my cause is assured.

sentences.zh: 秀實曰：「將士東征，宴賜不豐，有司過耳，人主何與知？

translations.literal: Xiushi said, "The officers and soldiers marched east; the feast rewards were not ample—that is the fault of the officials; what has the sovereign to do with knowing it?
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi said, "The troops marched east and were poorly rewarded at the feast—that is the officials' fault. What has the Son of Heaven to do with it?

sentences.zh: 公本以忠義聞天下，今變起倉卒，當諭眾以禍福，掃清宮室，迎乘輿，公之職也。」

translations.literal: You were originally known throughout the realm for loyalty and righteousness; now that disturbance has arisen in haste, you should instruct the multitude in fortune and misfortune, sweep clean the palace chambers, and welcome the imperial carriage—that is your duty."
translations.idiomatic: You are known throughout the realm for loyalty. Now that crisis has struck, you should explain the stakes to the troops, purge the palace, and welcome back the emperor. That is your duty."

sentences.zh: 泚默然。

translations.literal: Ci was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Ci said nothing.

sentences.zh: 秀實知不可，乃陽與合，陰結將軍劉海賓、姚令言、都虞候何明禮，欲圖泚。

translations.literal: Xiushi knew it would not do; he then outwardly joined Ci while secretly joining with Generals Liu Haibin, Yao Lingyan, and chief military police officer He Mingli, intending to plot against Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing persuasion had failed, Xiushi feigned compliance while secretly plotting with Generals Liu Haibin and Yao Lingyan and chief military police officer He Mingli to overthrow Ci.

sentences.zh: 三人者，皆秀實素所厚。

translations.literal: These three men were all long favored by Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: All three were men Xiushi had long favored.

sentences.zh: 會源休教泚偽迎天子，遣將韓旻領銳師三千疾馳奉天。

translations.literal: Just then Yuan Xiu taught Ci to feign welcoming the Son of Heaven and sent General Han Min to lead three thousand elite troops in rapid march to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu then urged Ci to feign welcoming the emperor and sent General Han Min with three thousand elite troops racing toward Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 秀實以為宗社之危不容喘，乃遣人諭大吏岐靈嶽竊取令言印，不獲，乃倒用司農印追其兵。

translations.literal: Xiushi considered that the peril to the altars of state allowed no pause for breath; he sent someone to instruct senior clerk Qi Lingyue to steal Lingyan's seal—this failed—so he used the Director of Granaries seal in reverse to recall the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi saw that the dynasty's peril brooked no delay. He sent word to senior clerk Qi Lingyue to steal Lingyan's seal; when that failed, he used the Director of Granaries seal to issue a recall order.

sentences.zh: 旻至駱驛，得符還。

translations.literal: Min reached Luoyi Post Station, obtained the tally, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Min reached Luoyi Post Station, received the recall order, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 秀實謂海賓曰：「旻之來，吾等無遺類。

translations.literal: Xiushi said to Haibin, "When Min comes, we shall leave no survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi told Haibin, "When Min returns, none of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 我當直搏殺賊，不然則死。」

translations.literal: I shall directly grapple and kill the traitor; if not, then die.
translations.idiomatic: I will strike Ci down myself, or die in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 乃約事急為繼，而令明禮應於外。

translations.literal: He then agreed that when the affair grew urgent they would follow up, and ordered Mingli to respond from outside.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed that when the moment came the others would follow up, with Mingli responding from outside.

sentences.zh: 翌日，泚召秀實計事，源休、姚令言、李忠臣、李子平皆在坐。

translations.literal: The next day Ci summoned Xiushi to discuss affairs; Yuan Xiu, Yao Lingyan, Li Zhongchen, and Li Ziping were all seated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ci summoned Xiushi to discuss strategy. Yuan Xiu, Yao Lingyan, Li Zhongchen, and Li Ziping were all present.

sentences.zh: 秀實戎服與休並語，至僭位，勃然起，執休腕，奪其象笏，奮而前，唾泚面大罵曰：「狂賊！

translations.literal: Xiushi in military dress spoke with Xiu side by side; when it came to usurping the throne, he suddenly rose, seized Xiu's wrist, snatched his ivory tablet, rushed forward, spat in Ci's face and cursed loudly, "Mad traitor!
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi in military dress sat with Xiu discussing the usurpation. He suddenly rose, seized Xiu's wrist, snatched his ivory tablet, rushed forward, spat in Ci's face, and roared, "Mad traitor!

sentences.zh: 可磔萬段，我豈從汝反邪！」

translations.literal: You deserve to be dismembered in ten thousand pieces—how could I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: You deserve to be torn limb from limb! Do you think I would follow you in rebellion?

sentences.zh: 遂擊之。

translations.literal: He then struck him.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Ci.

sentences.zh: 泚舉臂捍笏，中顙，流血衊面，匍匐走。

translations.literal: Ci raised his arm to ward off the tablet; it struck his forehead; blood flowed and spattered his face; he crawled away.
translations.idiomatic: Ci raised his arm to block the blow. The tablet struck his forehead, blood spattered his face, and he crawled away.

sentences.zh: 賊眾未敢動，而海賓等無至者。

translations.literal: The traitor host did not dare move, but Haibin and the others did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dared not move, but Haibin and the others never came.

sentences.zh: 秀實大呼曰：「我不同反，胡不殺我！」

translations.literal: Xiushi shouted loudly, "I do not join in rebellion—why not kill me!
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi shouted, "I will not rebel with you—why not kill me!

sentences.zh: 遂遇害，年六十五。

translations.literal: He was thereupon killed; he was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was cut down. He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 海賓、明禮、靈嶽等皆繼為賊害。

translations.literal: Haibin, Mingli, Lingyue, and the others were all in turn harmed by the traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Haibin, Mingli, Lingyue, and the others were killed in turn by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝在奉天，恨用秀實不極才，垂涕悔悵。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Fengtian; he regretted not employing Xiushi to the full extent of his talent, and shed tears in sorrow and remorse.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian the emperor wept in remorse, lamenting that he had never used Xiushi to the full measure of his ability.

sentences.zh: 初，秀實自涇州被召，戒其家曰：「若過岐，硃泚必致贈遺，慎毋納。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiushi was summoned from Jing Prefecture, he warned his household, "If we pass through Qi, Zhu Ci will surely send gifts—be careful not to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned from Jing, Xiushi warned his household, "If we pass through Qi, Zhu Ci will surely send gifts. Accept nothing.

sentences.zh: 至岐，泚固致大綾三百，家人拒，不遂。

translations.literal: When they reached Qi, Ci insistently sent three hundred bolts of fine silk; the household refused and he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi, Ci pressed three hundred bolts of fine silk on them. The household refused, and he failed.

sentences.zh: 至都，秀實怒曰：「吾終不以汙吾第。」

translations.literal: When they reached the capital, Xiushi said angrily, "I will never let this defile my residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital Xiushi said angrily, "I will never let this defile my home.

sentences.zh: 以置司農治堂之梁間。

translations.literal: He had it placed between the beams of the Director of Granaries' main hall.
translations.idiomatic: He had it stored between the beams of the Director of Granaries' main hall.

sentences.zh: 吏後以告泚，泚取視，其封帕完新。

translations.literal: Later a clerk reported this to Ci; Ci took it to look—the wrapping cloth was intact and new.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk later told Ci, who came to inspect it. The wrapping was still intact and untouched.

sentences.zh: 秀實嘗以禁兵寡弱，不足備非常，言於帝曰：「古者天子曰萬乘，諸侯曰千乘，大夫曰百乘，蓋以大制小，以十制一。

translations.literal: Xiushi once said that the imperial guard was few and weak, insufficient to meet emergencies, and told the emperor, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven was called 'ten thousand chariots,' feudal lords 'a thousand chariots,' grandees 'a hundred chariots'—this was to use the large to control the small, and ten to control one.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi once warned the emperor that the imperial guard was too few and weak to meet emergencies: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven was called 'ten thousand chariots,' lords 'a thousand chariots,' and grandees 'a hundred chariots'—the large controls the small, and ten controls one.

sentences.zh: 今外有不廷之虜，內有梗命之臣，而禁兵寡少，卒有患難，何以待之？

translations.literal: Now outside there are barbarians who do not attend court, inside there are ministers who resist orders, yet the imperial guard is few—if trouble suddenly arises, how will you meet it?
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians defy us outside, defiant ministers plot inside, yet the guard is pitifully small. When crisis strikes, how will you meet it?

sentences.zh: 且猛虎所以百獸畏者，為爪牙也；

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason the fierce tiger makes all beasts fear is its claws and fangs;
translations.idiomatic: A tiger terrifies all beasts because of its claws and fangs;

sentences.zh: 若去之，則犬彘馬牛，皆能為敵。」

translations.literal: if these are removed, then dogs, pigs, horses, and oxen can all become enemies.
translations.idiomatic: remove them, and dogs and pigs become its enemies.

sentences.zh: 帝不用。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 及涇卒亂，召神策六軍，無一人至者，世多其謀。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops mutinied and the Six Divine Strategy Armies were summoned, not one man came; the age greatly valued his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing troops mutinied and the Six Divine Strategy Armies were summoned, not one soldier came. The world then praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，詔贈太尉，諡曰忠烈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, an edict posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan (784), an edict posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 賜封戶五百，莊、第各一區；

translations.literal: He was granted a fief of five hundred households, one manor and one residence;
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a fief of five hundred households, a manor, and a residence;

sentences.zh: 長子三品，諸子五品，並正員官。

translations.literal: the eldest son third rank, the other sons fifth rank, all regular appointees.
translations.idiomatic: his eldest son third rank, his other sons fifth rank, all as regular appointees.

sentences.zh: 帝還都，又詔致祭，旌其門閭，親銘其碑雲。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, he again ordered sacrifices offered, honored his gate and lane, and personally inscribed his stele.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he ordered sacrifices, honored his household gate, and personally inscribed his stele.

sentences.zh: 太和中，子伯倫始立廟，有詔給鹵簿，賜度支綾絹五百，以少牢致祭。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, his son Bolun first established a temple; there was an edict granting imperial insignia, bestowing five hundred bolts of silk from the treasury, and offering sacrifice with the lesser tai la victims.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era his son Bolun first established a ancestral temple. An edict granted imperial insignia, five hundred bolts of treasury silk, and sacrifices with the lesser tai la victims.

sentences.zh: 伯倫累官福建觀察使，終太僕卿。

translations.literal: Bolun rose through offices to Fujian observation commissioner and ended as Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Bolun rose to Fujian observation commissioner and ended his career as Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 時宰相李石請文宗加賻襚，鄭覃曰：「自古殺身利社稷，未有如秀實者。」

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Li Shi asked Emperor Wenzong to add funeral gifts and shrouds; Zheng Tan said, "From antiquity, none who gave their lives for the altars of state has been like Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Shi asked Emperor Wenzong to add funeral gifts. Zheng Tan said, "From antiquity, none who gave his life for the state has equaled Xiushi.

sentences.zh: 帝惻然，為罷朝，可其請。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to compassion, dismissed court for it, and approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved, dismissed court, and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 孫嶷、文楚、珂知名。

translations.literal: Grandsons Yi, Wenchu, and Ke were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Yi, Wenchu, and Ke were well known.

sentences.zh: 孫 嶷嶷自鄭滑節度使入為右金吾衛大將軍，封西平郡公。

translations.literal: Grandson Yi: Yi came from Zheng-Hua military commissioner to enter office as Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Yi entered court from Zheng-Hua military commissioner as Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard and was enfeoffed Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 甘露之變，嶷當誅，裴度奏忠臣後，宜免死，貶循州司馬。

translations.literal: At the Sweet Dew Incident, Yi was due for execution; Pei Du memorialized that as descendant of a loyal minister he should be spared death and was demoted to prefectural marshal of Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the Sweet Dew Incident, Yi faced execution. Pei Du argued that as descendant of a loyal minister he should be spared and had him demoted to marshal of Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孫 文楚文楚，咸通末為雲州防禦使。

translations.literal: Grandson Wenchu: Wenchu, at the end of Xiantong, was defense commissioner of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Wenchu served as defense commissioner of Yun Prefecture at the end of the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 時李國昌鎮振武，國昌子克用欲得雲中，引兵攻之，殺於鬥雞台下，沙陀之亂自此始。

translations.literal: At the time Li Guochang held Zhenwu; Guochang's son Keyong wished to take Yunzhong, led troops to attack, and killed him below the Cockfighting Terrace—the Shatuo disorders began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guochang held Zhenwu; his son Keyong wanted Yunzhong, attacked, and killed Wenchu below the Cockfighting Terrace. The Shatuo disorders began here.

sentences.zh: 孫 珂珂，僖宗時居潁州。

translations.literal: Grandson Ke: Ke, in the time of Emperor Xizong, resided at Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Ke lived at Ying Prefecture under Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 黃巢圍潁，刺史欲以城降，珂募少年拒戰，眾裹糧請從，賊遂潰，拜州司馬。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao besieged Ying, the prefect wished to surrender the city; Ke recruited young men to resist; the multitude wrapped provisions and asked to follow; the bandits thereupon collapsed; he was appointed prefectural marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao besieged Ying, the prefect wished to surrender. Ke recruited young men to resist. Townspeople brought provisions and volunteered to fight. The rebels broke and fled. Ke was appointed prefectural marshal.

sentences.zh: 附 劉海賓劉海賓者，彭城人，以義俠聞。

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Haibin—Liu Haibin was a man of Pengcheng, renowned for righteous chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Liu Haibin of Pengcheng was renowned for righteous chivalry.

sentences.zh: 為涇原兵馬將，與秀實友善。

translations.literal: He was a Jingyuan troop-and-horse officer and was friendly with Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Jingyuan troop-and-horse officer and a close friend of Xiushi.

sentences.zh: 累戰功，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He accumulated battle merit and was concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated battle honors and was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 劉文喜據涇州叛，海賓與其子光國紿以奏請。

translations.literal: When Liu Wenxi held Jing Prefecture in rebellion, Haibin and his son Guangguo deceived him with a request for memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wenxi rebelled and held Jing, Haibin and his son Guangguo tricked him with a request to memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 及入對，因言奸慝可誅狀。

translations.literal: When they entered for audience, they thereupon spoke of the traitor's punishable guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At court they denounced the traitor's crimes and called for his execution.

sentences.zh: 既還，光國手斬文喜獻闕下，拜左驍衛大將軍，封五原郡王；

translations.literal: After returning, Guangguo personally beheaded Wenxi and presented him below the palace gates; he was appointed Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Wuyuan Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: On their return Guangguo personally beheaded Wenxi and presented his head at court. He was appointed Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and enfeoffed Prince of Wuyuan;

sentences.zh: 海賓樂平郡王，贈太子太保，實封百戶。

translations.literal: Haibin was made Prince of Leping Commandery, posthumously gifted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Haibin was made Prince of Leping, posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿，字清臣，秘書監師古五世從孫。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing, styled Qingchen, was the fifth-generation collateral descendant of Secretariat Director Yan Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, whose courtesy name was Qingchen, was a fifth-generation descendant of Secretariat Director Yan Shigu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母殷躬加訓導。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his mother Yin personally added instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised and taught by his mother, Lady Yin.

sentences.zh: 既長，博學工辭章，事親孝。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition, and filial in serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up, he became broadly learned and skilled in letters, and deeply filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 開元中，舉進士，又擢制科。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination and was also selected in the special decree examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination and was also selected in the special decree examination.

sentences.zh: 調醴泉尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Liquan.

sentences.zh: 再遷監察御史，使河、隴。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to investigating censor and sent to the He and Long circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor and sent on mission to the He and Long circuits.

sentences.zh: 時五原有冤獄久不決，天且旱，真卿辨獄而雨，郡人呼「御史雨」。

translations.literal: At the time Wuyuan had a wrongful case long unresolved; heaven was about to be dry; Zhenqing judged the case and rain fell; the commandery people called him "Censor Rain."
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyuan a wrongful case had long gone unresolved while drought threatened. Zhenqing cleared the case and rain fell. The people called him "Censor Rain."

sentences.zh: 復使河東，劾奏朔方令鄭延祚母死不葬三十年，有詔終身不齒，聞者聳然。

translations.literal: He was again sent to Hedong and impeached Shuo Prefecture magistrate Zheng Yanzuo for his mother's death unburied for thirty years; there was an edict that he never be ranked among officials for life; hearers were struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: Sent again to Hedong, he impeached Shuo magistrate Zheng Yanzuo for leaving his mother's body unburied for thirty years. An edict barred him from office for life. All who heard it were stunned.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時御史吉溫以私怨構中丞宋渾，謫賀州，真卿曰：「奈何以一時忿，欲危宋璟後乎？」

translations.literal: At the time Censor Ji Wen, from private resentment, framed Vice Censor Song Hun for demotion to He Prefecture; Zhenqing said, "How can you, for a moment's anger, wish to endanger the descendants of Song Jing?
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ji Wen framed Vice Censor Song Hun out of private spite and had him demoted to He Prefecture. Zhenqing said, "How can you, in a fit of anger, seek to destroy the descendants of Song Jing?

sentences.zh: 宰相楊國忠惡之，諷中丞蔣冽奏為東都採訪判官，再轉武部員外郎。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yang Guozhong hated him and prompted Vice Censor Jiang Lie to memorialize appointing him as Eastern Capital investigation staff judge; he was again transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Guozhong hated him and had Vice Censor Jiang Lie memorialize his transfer to Eastern Capital investigation staff judge, then to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 國忠終欲去之，乃出為平原太守。

translations.literal: Guozhong ultimately wished to remove him and sent him out as prefect of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong finally got rid of him by sending him out as prefect of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 安祿山逆狀牙孽，真卿度必反，陽托霖雨，增陴浚隍，料才壯，儲廥廩。

translations.literal: An Lushan's rebellious signs were sprouting like fangs; Zhenqing judged he would surely rebel; outwardly he pleaded continuous rain, raised walls and deepened moats, assessed strong men, and stored granaries.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan's rebellious intent was already showing. Zhenqing judged he would surely rebel. Outwardly citing heavy rains, he raised walls, deepened moats, assessed able men, and stocked granaries.

sentences.zh: 日與賓客泛舟飲酒，以紓祿山之疑。

translations.literal: Daily he went boating and drinking wine with guests to ease Lushan's suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days boating and drinking with guests to allay Lushan's suspicions.

sentences.zh: 果以為書生，不虞也。

translations.literal: Lushan indeed took him for a bookish man and did not guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan took him for a mere scholar and never suspected him.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，河朔盡陷，獨平原城守具備，使司兵參軍李平馳奏。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, the north of the Yellow River fell entirely; only Pingyuan's defenses and stores were complete; he sent staff officer Li Ping in rapid memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, every prefecture north of the Yellow River fell—only Pingyuan stood ready. Zhenqing sent staff officer Li Ping racing to court with the news.

sentences.zh: 玄宗始聞亂，歎曰：「河北二十四郡，無一忠臣邪？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong first heard of the rebellion, he sighed and said, "Of the twenty-four commanderies of Hebei, is there not one loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong first heard of the rebellion, he sighed: "Of Hebei's twenty-four commanderies, is there not one loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 及平至，帝大喜，謂左右曰：「朕不識真卿何如人，所為乃若此！」

translations.literal: When Ping arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased and said to those at his side, "I did not know what sort of man Zhenqing was—his conduct is like this!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ping arrived, the emperor was overjoyed and said to his attendants, "I never knew what manner of man Zhenqing was—and see what he has done!"

translations.literal: Closing mark of direct speech.
translations.idiomatic: End of the emperor's words.

sentences.zh: 時平原有靜塞兵三千，乃益募士，得萬人，遣錄事參軍李擇交統之，以刁萬歲、和琳、徐浩、馬相如、高抗朗等為將，分總部伍。

translations.literal: At the time Pingyuan had three thousand Jingsai troops; he then further recruited men and obtained ten thousand, sent recording officer Li Zejiao to command them, and made Diao Wansui, He Lin, Xu Hao, Ma Xiangru, Gao Kanglang, and others generals to divide command of the units.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan had three thousand Jingsai troops. Zhenqing recruited until he had ten thousand men, put recording officer Li Zejiao in overall command, and appointed Diao Wansui, He Lin, Xu Hao, Ma Xiangru, Gao Kanglang, and others as generals to lead the units.

sentences.zh: 大饗士城西門，慷慨泣下，眾感勵。

translations.literal: He held a great feast for the soldiers at the west gate, wept passionately, and the multitude was moved and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: At the west gate he treated his troops to a great banquet, weeping as he spoke with passion until all were stirred to renewed courage.

sentences.zh: 饒陽太守盧全誠、濟南太守李隨、清河長史王懷忠、景城司馬李暐、鄴郡太守王燾各以眾歸，有詔北海太守賀蘭進明率精銳五千濟河為助。

translations.literal: Raoyang Prefect Lu Quancheng, Jinan Prefect Li Sui, Qinghe Chief Administrator Wang Huaizhong, Jingcheng Assistant Commander Li Wei, and Ye Prefecture Prefect Wang Tao each came over with their forces; an edict ordered Beihai Prefect Helan Jinming to lead five thousand picked troops across the river to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Raoyang's Lu Quancheng, Jinan's Li Sui, Qinghe chief administrator Wang Huaizhong, Jingcheng's Li Wei, and Ye's Wang Tao all defected with their men. The court ordered Beihai prefect Helan Jinming to cross the Yellow River with five thousand crack troops to aid him.

sentences.zh: 賊破東都，遣段子光傳李憕、盧奕、蔣清首徇河北，真卿畏眾懼，紿諸將曰：「吾素識憕等，其首皆非是。」

translations.literal: The rebels took the Eastern Capital and sent Duan Ziguang to parade the heads of Li Zhi, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing through Hebei; Zhenqing feared the troops would panic and deceived the generals, saying, "I have long known Zhi and the others—these heads are none of them real."
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels captured Luoyang, they sent Duan Ziguang to display the severed heads of Li Zhi, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing across Hebei. Fearing his men would lose heart, Zhenqing lied to his officers: "I knew Zhi and the others well—these heads are not theirs.

sentences.zh: 乃斬子光，藏三首。

translations.literal: He then executed Ziguang and concealed the three heads.
translations.idiomatic: With that he had Ziguang beheaded and hid the three heads from view.

sentences.zh: 它日，結芻續體，斂而祭，為位哭之。

translations.literal: On another day, he bound straw into figures to complete the bodies, gathered them for burial rites, set out mourning places, and wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he had straw figures fashioned to stand in for the missing bodies, interred them with proper rites, arranged mourning seats, and led the lamentation.

sentences.zh: 是時，從父兄杲卿為常山太守，斬賊將李欽湊等，清土門。

translations.literal: At this time his paternal cousin Gaoqing was Prefect of Changshan; he beheaded the rebel generals Li Qintou and others and cleared Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: About then his cousin Gaoqing, as prefect of Changshan, killed the rebel commanders Li Qintou and his fellows and reclaimed Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 十七郡同日自歸，推真卿為盟主，兵二十萬，絕燕、趙。

translations.literal: Seventeen commanderies on the same day submitted of their own accord; they made Zhenqing covenant leader, with two hundred thousand troops cutting off Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On a single day seventeen commanderies came over to the loyal side and chose Zhenqing as their alliance chief. With two hundred thousand men he severed rebel communications between Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 詔即拜戶部侍郎，佐李光弼討賊。

translations.literal: An edict immediately appointed him Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue to assist Li Guangbi in suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The throne at once made him vice minister of revenue to serve under Li Guangbi against the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 真卿以李暉自副，而用李銑、賈載、沈震為判官。

translations.literal: Zhenqing took Li Hui as his deputy and employed Li Xian, Jia Zai, and Shen Zhen as staff judges.
translations.idiomatic: He made Li Hui his second-in-command and appointed Li Xian, Jia Zai, and Shen Zhen as his staff officers.

sentences.zh: 俄加河北招討採訪使。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Hebei Pacification and Investigation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also named commissioner for pacification and inspection in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 清河太守使郡人李崿來乞師，崿曰：「聞公首奮裾唱大順，河朔恃公為金城。

translations.literal: The Prefect of Qinghe sent a man of the commandery, Li E, to beg for troops; E said, "I hear that you were first to stir your robes and proclaim the Great Cause; the region north of the river relies on you as a golden fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe's prefect dispatched a local man named Li E to request reinforcements. E said: "Word has spread that you were the first in Hebei to raise the banner of loyalty. All the north now treats you as their bulwark.

sentences.zh: 清河，西鄰也，有江淮租布備北軍，號'天下北庫'。

translations.literal: Qinghe, a western neighbor, holds grain rents and cloth tribute from the Jianghuai stored for the northern armies—called 'Treasury of the North Under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe lies on your western flank. It holds Jianghuai grain and cloth reserves for the northern armies—known as the empire's northern storehouse.

sentences.zh: 計其積，足以三平原之有，士卒可以二平原之眾。

translations.literal: Counting its stores, they are enough to triple what Pingyuan possesses; its soldiers can match twice Pingyuan's numbers.
translations.idiomatic: By its stockpiles alone it could supply three times what you have in Pingyuan, and its troops would more than double your current strength.

sentences.zh: 公因而撫有，以為腹心，它城運之如臂之指耳。」

translations.literal: If Your Lordship takes and holds it thereby as your vital core, other cities will move at your bidding like fingers on an arm."
translations.idiomatic: Seize it and make it your strategic heartland, and every other city will answer your orders as readily as fingers move at a gesture of the hand.

sentences.zh: 真卿為出兵六千，謂曰：「吾兵已出，子將何以教我？」

translations.literal: Zhenqing thereupon dispatched six thousand troops and said to him, "My soldiers have already marched out—what counsel will you give me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing sent six thousand men and asked him: "My troops are on the move—what do you propose we do next?

sentences.zh: 崿曰：「朝家使程千里統眾十萬，自太行而東，將出槨口，限賊不得前。

translations.literal: E said, "The court has sent Cheng Qianli to command one hundred thousand men east from the Taihang Mountains; he will soon emerge at Guo Pass and block the rebels from advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Li E replied: "The throne has Cheng Qianli leading a hundred thousand men eastward through the Taihang range. He means to debouch at Guo Pass and pin the rebels in place.

sentences.zh: 公若先伐魏郡，斬賊守袁知泰，以勁兵披郭口，出官師使討鄴、幽陵，平原、清河合十萬眾徇洛陽，分犀銳制其沖。

translations.literal: If Your Lordship first attacks Wei Commandery, beheads the rebel defender Yuan Zhita, breaks through with elite troops at Guo Pass, sends the imperial army to strike Ye and Youling, joins Pingyuan and Qinghe in one hundred thousand men to advance on Luoyang, and splits off crack troops to control their choke points—
translations.idiomatic: If you strike Wei first, kill the rebel garrison commander Yuan Zhita, punch through Guo Pass with your best units, and dispatch the imperial forces against Ye and Youbei while Pingyuan and Qinghe combine a hundred thousand men to threaten Luoyang, then detach elite troops to hold the enemy's vital crossings—

sentences.zh: 公堅壁勿與戰，不數十日，賊必潰，相圖死。」

translations.literal: Your Lordship hold fast behind walls and do not give battle; within fewer than ten days the rebels will surely collapse and turn on one another to the death."
translations.idiomatic: hold your lines and refuse battle. Within ten days their army will break apart and they will destroy each other.

sentences.zh: 真卿然之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing agreed that this was the plan.

sentences.zh: 乃檄清河等郡，遣大將李擇交、副將范冬馥、和琳、徐浩與清河、博平士五千屯堂邑。

translations.literal: He thereupon issued proclamations to Qinghe and other commanderies, dispatched the great general Li Zejiao, deputy generals Fan Dongfu, He Lin, and Xu Hao with five thousand men of Qinghe and Boping to encamp at Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He notified Qinghe and neighboring commanderies, then sent his chief general Li Zejiao with deputies Fan Dongfu, He Lin, and Xu Hao and five thousand troops from Qinghe and Boping to garrison Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 袁知泰遣將白嗣深、乙舒蒙等兵二萬拒戰，賊敗，斬首萬級，知泰走汲郡。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhita sent the generals Bai Sishen, Yi Shumeng, and others with twenty thousand troops to resist; the rebels were defeated, ten thousand heads were taken, and Zhita fled to Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhita met them with twenty thousand men under Bai Sishen and Yi Shumeng. The rebels were routed; ten thousand were killed or captured, and Zhita fled to Ji.

sentences.zh: 史思明圍饒陽，遣游奕兵絕平原救軍，真卿懼不敵，以書招賀蘭進明，以河北招討使讓之。

translations.literal: Shi Siming besieged Raoyang and sent roving patrol troops to cut off Pingyuan's relief army; Zhenqing feared he could not match them and wrote summoning Helan Jinming, reproaching him as Hebei Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming blockaded Raoyang and sent mobile units to intercept relief from Pingyuan. Convinced he was outmatched, Zhenqing wrote to Helan Jinming, upbraiding him in his capacity as Hebei pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進明敗於信都。

translations.literal: Jinming was defeated at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming was beaten at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 會平盧將劉正臣以漁陽歸，真卿欲堅其意，遣賈載越海遺軍資十余萬，以子頗為質。

translations.literal: When Pinglu general Liu Zhengchen submitted Yuyang, Zhenqing wished to strengthen his resolve; he sent Jia Zai across the sea with more than one hundred thousand in military supplies and offered his son Po as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengchen of Pinglu had just brought Yuyang over to the loyal side. To cement his commitment, Zhenqing sent Jia Zai by sea with military supplies worth more than a hundred thousand cash—and pledged his son Po as surety.

sentences.zh: 頗甫十歲，軍中固請留之，不從。

translations.literal: Po was just ten years old; the army firmly asked to retain him, but [Zhenqing] did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Po was only ten. His officers begged him to keep the boy back, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 肅宗已即位靈武，真卿數遣使以蠟丸裹書陳事。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong had already ascended at Lingwu; Zhenqing repeatedly sent envoys bearing letters wrapped in wax pellets to lay out affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Suzong had taken the throne at Lingwu. Zhenqing sent messenger after messenger with wax-sealed dispatches reporting on conditions in the north.

sentences.zh: 拜工部尚書兼御史大夫，復為河北招討使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and again made Hebei Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of works and chief censor, and once more named Hebei pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時軍費困竭，李崿勸真卿收景城鹽，使諸郡相輸，用度遂不乏。

translations.literal: At the time military funds were exhausted; Li E urged Zhenqing to collect salt from Jingcheng and have the commanderies contribute to one another, and expenditures were thereafter never wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Military funds were running dry. Li E persuaded Zhenqing to monopolize Jingcheng salt and arrange mutual deliveries among the commanderies. From then on supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 第五琦方參進明軍，後得其法以行，軍用饒雄。

translations.literal: Diwu Qi was then attached to Jinming's army; later he obtained this method and applied it, and military supplies became abundant and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Qi was then serving in Jinming's command. He later adopted the same scheme on a wider scale, and the imperial armies grew flush with resources.

sentences.zh: 祿山乘虛遣思明、尹子奇急攻河北，諸郡復陷，獨平原、博平、清河固守。

translations.literal: Lushan seized the opening to dispatch Siming and Yin Ziqi in urgent attacks on Hebei; the commanderies again fell, and only Pingyuan, Boping, and Qinghe held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan seized the moment to hurl Siming and Yin Ziqi against Hebei. The commanderies fell again one by one; only Pingyuan, Boping, and Qinghe held out.

sentences.zh: 然人心危，不復振。

translations.literal: Yet men's hearts were fearful and no longer revived.
translations.idiomatic: Morale nonetheless collapsed, and the will to fight did not return.

sentences.zh: 真卿謀於眾曰：「賊銳甚，不可抗。

translations.literal: Zhenqing consulted the assembly, saying, "The rebels are very sharp—we cannot resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing consulted his officers: "The enemy is too strong for us to stand against.

sentences.zh: 若委命辱國，非計也。

translations.literal: To consign our lives and disgrace the state is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: To die here and disgrace the empire serves no purpose.

sentences.zh: 不如徑赴行在，朝廷若誅敗軍罪，吾死不恨。」

translations.literal: Better to go straight to the mobile court; if the court condemns us for defeat, I will die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Better to make our way directly to the emperor's camp. If the court holds us accountable for losing the north, I will accept death without regret.

sentences.zh: 至德元載十月，棄郡度河，間關至鳳翔謁帝，詔授憲部尚書，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Zhide, he abandoned the commandery, crossed the river, and after trials reached Fengxiang to audience with the emperor; an edict appointed him Minister of Justice, and he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhide 1 (756), he abandoned his post, crossed the Yellow River, and after a perilous journey reached Fengxiang to see the emperor. The court made him minister of justice, then chief censor.

sentences.zh: 方朝廷草昧不暇給，而真卿繩治如平日。

translations.literal: Just as the court was in its founding chaos and had no leisure to spare, Zhenqing enforced discipline as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Even while the court was still scrambling to establish itself, Zhenqing enforced order as rigorously as ever.

sentences.zh: 武部侍郎崔漪、諫議大夫李何忌皆被劾斥降。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Cui Yi and Remonstrance and Advice Grandee Li Heji were all impeached, expelled, and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yi, vice minister of war, and Li Heji, remonstrating advisor, were both impeached, dismissed, and demoted.

sentences.zh: 廣平王總兵二十萬平長安，辭日，當闕不敢乘，趨出枑乃乘。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping commanded two hundred thousand troops to pacify Chang'an; on the day of his farewell audience, facing the palace gate he dared not ride; only after hurrying past the barrier did he mount.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangping took leave to reconquer Chang'an at the head of two hundred thousand men, he dismounted before the palace gate and did not remount until he had passed beyond the barrier.

sentences.zh: 王府都虞候管崇嗣先王而騎，真卿劾之。

translations.literal: The prince's household Chief Commandant Guan Chongsi rode ahead of the prince; Zhenqing impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Chongsi, chief commandant of the prince's household guard, rode out ahead of his lord. Zhenqing censured him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝還奏，慰答曰：「朕子每出，諄諄教戒，故不敢失。

translations.literal: The emperor returned his memorial and replied in consolation, "Each time my son goes out, I earnestly teach and warn him—thus he dares not err.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned his memorial with a placating reply: "I instruct my son carefully whenever he leaves court. That is why he was so careful.

sentences.zh: 崇嗣老而鐍，卿姑容之。」

translations.literal: Chongsi is old and dull—my lord, for now tolerate him."
translations.idiomatic: Chongsi is old and slow-witted—for now, let it pass.

sentences.zh: 百官肅然。

translations.literal: The hundred officials were awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the whole court stood in awe of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 兩京復，帝遺左司郎中李選告宗廟，祝署「嗣皇帝」，真卿謂禮儀使崔器曰：「上皇在蜀，可乎？」

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, the emperor sent Left Directorate Gentleman Li Xuan to announce at the ancestral temple; the prayer text was signed "Succession Emperor"; Zhenqing said to Ceremonial Commissioner Cui Qi, "The Retired Emperor is in Shu—can this be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an and Luoyang were retaken, the emperor sent Li Xuan of the left secretariat to report to the ancestral shrine. The prayer was signed "Succession Emperor." Zhenqing asked the master of ceremonies, Cui Qi: "The former emperor is still in Shu—how can this be right?

sentences.zh: 器遽奏改之，帝以為達識。

translations.literal: Qi hastily memorialized to change it; the emperor considered this discerning knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Qi immediately memorialized for a correction. The emperor praised his sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「《春秋》，新宮災，魯成公三日哭。

translations.literal: He further submitted advice: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when the new palace suffered fire, Duke Cheng of Lu mourned for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals record that when Duke Cheng of Lu's new palace burned, he mourned for three days.

sentences.zh: 今太廟為賊毀，請築壇于野，皇帝東向哭，然後遣使。」

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Ancestral Temple was destroyed by rebels—I ask that an altar be built in the open country, the emperor face east and weep, and only then dispatch envoys."
