translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple has been wrecked by the rebels. I propose that an altar be raised in the open, that His Majesty face east and weep for three days, and only then send envoys abroad.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: [The proposal] was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 宰相厭其言，出為馮翊太守。

translations.literal: The chief ministers grew weary of his words and had him sent out as Prefect of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers wearied of his admonitions and had him posted away as prefect of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 轉蒲州刺史，封丹陽縣子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Pu Prefecture and enfeoffed as Viscount of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Pu prefecture and ennobled as Viscount of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 為御史唐旻誣劾，貶饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Min falsely impeached him, and he was demoted to Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Min brought a trumped-up charge against him, and he was demoted to prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，拜浙西節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he was appointed military governor of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 劉展將反，真卿豫飭戰備，都統李峘以為生事，非短真卿，因召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan was about to rebel; Zhenqing made advance preparations for war; Supreme Commander Li Chan considered it troublemaking and not a shortcoming of Zhenqing; therefore he was summoned back as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan was plotting rebellion, Zhenqing had already begun preparing defenses. Supreme commander Li Chan regarded this as inflammatory rather than as a personal failing on Zhenqing's part, but recalled him to the capital as vice minister of justice anyway.

sentences.zh: 展卒舉兵度淮，而峘奔江西。

translations.literal: Zhan ultimately raised troops and crossed the Huai; Chan fled to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan did rebel and crossed the Huai River, and Li Chan fled into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 李輔國遷上皇西宮，真卿率百官問起居，輔國惡之，貶蓬州長史。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo moved the Retired Emperor to the Western Palace; Zhenqing led the hundred officials to inquire after his health; Fuguo hated this and demoted him to Chief Administrator of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fuguo installed the retired emperor in the Western Palace, Zhenqing led the entire court to inquire after his health. Fuguo resented the gesture and had him demoted to chief administrator of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，起為利州刺史，不拜，再遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended, he was promoted to Prefect of Lizhou but did not accept; he was again transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Daizong's accession he was offered Lizhou prefecture but declined. He was soon transferred again to vice minister of the civil service.

sentences.zh: 除荊南節度使，未行，改尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Jingnan; before he departed, [the appointment] was changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was named governor of Jingnan but never took up the post; instead he was made vice director of the right secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝自陝還，真卿請先謁陵廟而即宮，宰相元載以為迂，真卿怒曰：「用舍在公，言者何罪？

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Shanzhou, Zhenqing asked first to visit the tombs and temples and only then enter the palace; Chief Minister Yuan Zai considered this pedantic; Zhenqing angrily said, "Appointment and dismissal lie with Your Majesty—what crime is there in speaking?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shanzhou, Zhenqing urged that he visit the imperial tombs and shrines before entering the palace. Yuan Zai dismissed the suggestion as needlessly fussy. Zhenqing flared: "The throne decides who serves and who goes—what crime is there in offering counsel?

sentences.zh: 然朝廷事豈堪公再破壞邪！」

translations.literal: Yet how can the affairs of court endure Your Lordship wrecking them again!"
translations.idiomatic: But can the court survive your wrecking it a second time?

sentences.zh: 載銜之。

translations.literal: Zai bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai never forgave the rebuke.

sentences.zh: 俄以檢校刑部尚書為朔方行營宣慰使，未行，留知省事，更封魯郡公。

translations.literal: Before long, as Acting Minister of Justice he was made Pacification Commissioner of the Shuofang Field Headquarters; before departing he was retained to handle routine business and further enfeoffed as Duke of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named acting minister of justice and pacification commissioner for the Shuofang campaign, but never left the capital. He was kept on to manage routine affairs and ennobled again as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 時載多引私黨，畏群臣論奏，乃紿帝曰：「群臣奏事，多挾讒毀。

translations.literal: At the time Zai brought in many personal partisans; fearing that the ministers would discuss and memorialize, he deceived the emperor, saying, "When ministers submit affairs, they often carry slander and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was filling offices with his own men and feared open debate in court. He tricked the emperor: "Ministers who petition you often use their reports to spread slander.

sentences.zh: 請每論事，皆先白長官，長官以白宰相，宰相詳可否以聞。」

translations.literal: I ask that whenever affairs are discussed, one first inform one's superior; the superior inform the chief minister; the chief minister examine whether they may proceed and then report."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that every petition pass first to a man's department head, then to the chief minister, who will judge its merits before anything reaches Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 真卿上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zhenqing submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing answered with a memorial:

sentences.zh: 諸司長官者，達官也，皆得專達于天子。

translations.literal: The chiefs of the various bureaus are high officials, and each may report directly to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of the various departments are senior officials, each entitled to communicate directly with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 郎官、御史，陛下腹心耳目之臣也，故出使天下，事無細大得失，皆俾訪察，還以聞。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat and censors are Your Majesty's trusted eyes and ears; therefore they are sent throughout the realm, and whether matters are minor or major, gain or loss, all are ordered to investigate and report back.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and censors are your eyes and ears in the field. They are dispatched across the empire to investigate every matter, great or small, and report back to you.

sentences.zh: 此古明四目、達四聰也。

translations.literal: This is the ancient principle of making the four eyes clear and the four ears penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ancient ideal of extending sight and hearing in every direction.

sentences.zh: 今陛下欲自屏耳目，使不聰明，則天下何望焉？

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty wishes to screen off your own eyes and ears and make yourself unhearing and unseeing, upon what can the realm set its hopes?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now chooses to block your own eyes and ears and dull your understanding, what hope can the realm place in you?

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「營營青蠅，止於棘；

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Buzzing blue flies, alighting on the brambles;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says: "Buzzing blue flies, settling on the brambles;

sentences.zh: 讒言罔極，交亂四國。」

translations.literal: slanderous words without limit, crossing and confounding the four states."
translations.idiomatic: slander without end, sowing chaos among the four quarters of the realm.

sentences.zh: 以其能變白為黑，變黑為白也。

translations.literal: because they can turn white into black and black into white.
translations.idiomatic: Because slander can turn white into black and black into white.

sentences.zh: 詩人疾之，故曰：「取彼讒人，投畀豺虎；

translations.literal: The poet hated this, and therefore said: "Seize those slanderers and cast them to wolves and tigers;
translations.idiomatic: The poet despised them, and wrote: "Seize those slanderers and throw them to wolves and tigers;

sentences.zh: 豺虎不食，投畀有北。」

translations.literal: wolves and tigers will not eat them—cast them to the northern wastes."
translations.idiomatic: if wolves and tigers refuse them, cast them to the northern wilds.

sentences.zh: 昔夏之伯明、楚之無極、漢之江充，皆讒人也，陛下惡之，宜矣。

translations.literal: In antiquity Bo Ming of Xia, Wuji of Chu, and Jiang Chong of Han were all slanderers; that Your Majesty hates them is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Bo Ming of Xia, Wuji of Chu, and Jiang Chong of Han were all notorious slanderers. Your Majesty is right to despise such men.

sentences.zh: 胡不回神省察？

translations.literal: Why not turn your spirit and examine closely?
translations.idiomatic: Why not turn your mind to careful scrutiny instead?

sentences.zh: 其言虛誣，則讒人也，宜誅殛之；

translations.literal: If their words are false and deceitful, then they are slanderers and should be executed and destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: If a report proves false, its author is a slanderer and should be punished;

sentences.zh: 其言不誣，則正人也，宜獎勵之。

translations.literal: if their words are not false, then they are upright men and should be rewarded and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: if it proves true, its author is an upright man and should be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 舍此不為，使眾人謂陛下不能省察而倦聽覽，以是為辭，臣竊惜之。

translations.literal: To set this aside and not do it will make the multitude say that Your Majesty cannot examine closely and has grown weary of listening and reading—using this as a pretext; your servant privately regrets it.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this course and give people reason to say that Your Majesty will no longer examine reports or heed counsel—that, I deeply regret, is exactly the pretext being offered.

sentences.zh: 昔太宗勤勞庶政，其《司門式》曰：「無門籍者有急奏，令監司與仗家引對，不得關礙。」

translations.literal: In antiquity Emperor Taizong toiled diligently over the myriad affairs of government; his Regulations of the Gate Office say: "Those without gate registers who have urgent memorials—order the supervising officials and the guard household to lead them in audience; they must not be blocked or hindered."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once labored over every detail of government. His Gate Office regulations state: "Anyone without a gate pass who bears urgent business shall be escorted in for audience by the duty officers—no obstruction permitted.

sentences.zh: 防擁蔽也。

translations.literal: This guards against obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: That was to guard against blocking access to the throne.

sentences.zh: 置立仗馬二，須乘者聽。

translations.literal: He established two standing-duty horses; whoever needed to ride was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He even kept two horses saddled at the gate for any official who needed to ride in on urgent business.

sentences.zh: 此其平治天下也。

translations.literal: This was how he brought peace and order to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That is how he kept the realm at peace.

sentences.zh: 天寶後，李林甫得君，群臣不先咨宰相輒奏事者，托以他故中傷之，猶不敢明約百司，使先關白。

translations.literal: After the Tianbao era, when Li Linfu won the ruler's trust, ministers who submitted affairs without first consulting the chief minister were, on pretext of other causes, struck down and harmed; yet he still did not dare openly require all offices to give prior notice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era Li Linfu dominated the court. Officials who petitioned without consulting him first were destroyed on trumped-up charges—yet even he did not dare openly decree that every office must clear business with the chief minister first.

sentences.zh: 時閹人袁思藝日宣詔至中書，天子動靜必告林甫，林甫得以先意奏請，帝驚喜若神，故權寵日甚，道路以目。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Yuan Siyi daily announced edicts at the Secretariat; the Son of Heaven's every movement was reported to Linfu, and Linfu was able to anticipate his wishes in memorials; the emperor was delighted as if by divinity; therefore power and favor daily grew, and people on the road exchanged glances in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yuan Siyi brought the emperor's orders to the Secretariat each day, so Linfu always knew the ruler's mind before anyone else and could frame his proposals accordingly. The emperor marveled at his prescience. Linfu's power swelled, and people feared even to meet one another's eyes in the street.

sentences.zh: 上意不下宣，下情不上達，此權臣蔽主，不遵太宗之法也。

translations.literal: The ruler's intent was not proclaimed below, and sentiment below did not reach above—this is a powerful minister screening the ruler, not following Taizong's law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's will no longer reached the realm, and the realm's grievances no longer reached the emperor. That is how a powerful minister blinds his sovereign—and it departs from Taizong's way of rule.

sentences.zh: 陵夷至於今，天下之敝皆萃陛下，其所從來漸矣。

translations.literal: Decline continued down to the present; the realm's ills all converge upon Your Majesty—their origin has been gradual.
translations.idiomatic: The decay has continued to this day, and every affliction of the realm now falls upon Your Majesty. It did not happen all at once—it came by degrees.

sentences.zh: 自艱難之初，百姓尚未凋竭，太平之治猶可致，而李輔國當權，宰相用事，遞為姑息。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the hard trials, the common people had not yet been exhausted and depleted; rule of great peace could still be achieved—yet Li Fuguo held power, chief ministers wielded affairs, and each in turn practiced indulgent leniency.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the rebellion the people were not yet ruined and good government could still have been restored. Instead Li Fuguo seized power, and chief ministers who followed him indulged one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 開三司，誅反側，使餘賊潰將北走党項，裒嘯不逞，更相驚恐，思明危懼，相挻而反，東都陷沒，先帝由是憂勤損壽。

translations.literal: They opened the Three Offices, executed those of the opposing faction, causing remnant rebel routed generals to flee north to the Tangut tribes; bandits gathered and howled, unable to succeed, mutually alarming one another in fear; Siming grew fearful and perilous; they incited one another to rebel again; the Eastern Capital fell; the late emperor from this worried and toiled and shortened his lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: They established the Three Offices to try collaborators and executed those deemed disloyal, driving scattered rebel commanders north toward the Tangut tribes. Brigands roamed unchecked, terror fed on terror, and Siming, fearing for his life, rose again. Luoyang fell, and the late emperor wore himself down with grief until his health broke.

sentences.zh: 臣每思之，痛貫心骨。

translations.literal: Each time your servant thinks of it, pain pierces to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on this, grief pierces me to the bone.

sentences.zh: 今天下瘡痏未平，干戈日滋，陛下豈得不博聞讜言以廣視聽，而塞絕忠諫乎？

translations.literal: Today the realm's sores and wounds are not yet healed, and arms daily multiply—how can Your Majesty fail to broadly hear upright words to widen sight and hearing, yet instead block off loyal remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still bleeding from its wounds and war grows daily. How can Your Majesty refuse to broaden your hearing with honest counsel—and instead cut off loyal remonstrance?

sentences.zh: 陛下在陝時，奏事者不限貴賤，群臣以為太宗之治可跂而待。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was at Shanzhou, those submitting affairs were not limited by noble or base rank; the ministers considered that Taizong's governance could be awaited on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was at Shanzhou, anyone could petition regardless of rank, and the court believed Taizong's golden age was within reach.

sentences.zh: 且君子難進易退，朝廷開不諱之路，猶恐不言，況懷厭怠。

translations.literal: Moreover, for the noble man it is hard to advance and easy to withdraw; even when the court opens a path of no taboo, one still fears they will not speak—how much more when they harbor weariness and indolence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, upright men find it hard to speak up and easy to fall silent. Even when the court opens every avenue for frank speech, men still hesitate—how much more so when they sense indifference or hostility.

sentences.zh: 令宰相宣進止，御史台作條目，不得直進，從此人不奏事矣。

translations.literal: To order the chief minister to announce what may proceed or halt, and the Censorate to draw up regulations forbidding direct submission—from this people will no longer submit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If the chief minister alone decides what reaches you, and the Censorate writes rules barring direct access, from that day forward no one will petition at all.

sentences.zh: 陛下聞見，止於數人耳目。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's hearing and seeing will be limited to the eyes and ears of a few men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's knowledge of the realm will be confined to what a handful of men choose to tell you.

sentences.zh: 天下之士，方鉗口結舌，陛下便謂無事可論，豈知懼而不敢進，即林甫、國忠復起矣。

translations.literal: Men of talent throughout the realm are just now clamping their mouths and binding their tongues; Your Majesty then says there is nothing worth discussing—do you not know they fear and dare not advance? This is Linfu and Guozhong rising again.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent across the empire are already clamping shut their mouths. Your Majesty will conclude that nothing need be discussed—but they are silent from fear, not from contentment. This is how Linfu and Yang Guozhong rise again.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今日之事，曠古未有，雖林甫、國忠猶不敢公為之。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that today's affair is without precedent in all antiquity; even Linfu and Guozhong did not dare do it openly.
translations.idiomatic: I say that what is proposed today has no precedent in history. Even Linfu and Yang Guozhong never dared to do this openly.

sentences.zh: 陛下不早覺悟，漸成孤立，後悔無及矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not awaken early, you will gradually become isolated, and regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not see this now, you will gradually stand alone—and regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 於是中人等騰布中外。

translations.literal: Thereupon eunuchs spread the news inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs promptly spread word of the memorial throughout the palace and beyond.

sentences.zh: 後攝事太廟，言祭器不飭，載以為誹謗，貶峽州別駕。

translations.literal: Later, while acting in affairs at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he said the sacrificial vessels were not in proper order; Zai considered this slander and demoted him to Vice-Prefect of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while overseeing rites at the ancestral temple, he reported that the sacrificial vessels were ill kept. Zai treated this as slander and had him demoted to vice-prefect of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 改吉州司馬，遷撫、湖二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Military Administrator of Ji Prefecture, then transferred to Prefect of Fu and Hu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as military administrator of Jizhou, then promoted to prefect of Fu and Hu prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 載誅，楊綰薦之，擢刑部尚書，進吏部。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, Yang Wan recommended him; he was promoted to Minister of Justice and advanced to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Zai's execution Yang Wan recommended him. He was raised to minister of justice and then to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，以為禮儀使。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he was made Commissioner of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, he was appointed Commissioner of Rites.

sentences.zh: 因奏列聖諡繁，請從初議為定，袁傪固排之，罷不報。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that the posthumous titles of successive emperors were excessive and asked that the original proposals be taken as final; Yuan Cen firmly opposed it, and the matter was dropped without response.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the posthumous titles of successive emperors had grown excessive and asked that the original proposals stand. Yuan Cen blocked the request, and it was dropped without reply.

sentences.zh: 時喪亂後，典法湮放，真卿雖博識今古，屢建議釐正，為權臣沮抑，多中格雲。

translations.literal: At the time, after the disorders, canonical rites were lost and scattered; though Zhenqing was broadly learned in past and present, he repeatedly proposed corrections, but was obstructed by powerful ministers and many proposals were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: After the civil wars, ritual law lay in ruins. Though Zhenqing was deeply learned and repeatedly proposed corrections, powerful ministers blocked him and most of his proposals never took effect.

sentences.zh: 楊炎當國，以直不容，換太子少師，然猶領使。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan held the state, because his uprightness was not tolerated, he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, yet still headed the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan dominated the government, his blunt integrity could not be tolerated. He was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent but still headed the rites commission.

sentences.zh: 及盧杞，益不喜，改太子太師，並使罷之，數遣人問方鎮所便，將出之。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi came to power, he liked him still less, changed him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and also had him dismissed from the commission; he repeatedly sent men to ask which frontier command suited him, intending to send him out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Lu Qi he fared worse still. Qi made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, stripped him of the rites commission, and repeatedly asked which frontier post would suit him, clearly intending to exile him.

sentences.zh: 真卿往見杞，辭曰：「先中丞傳首平原，面流血，吾不敢以衣拭，親舌舐之，公忍不見容乎！」

translations.literal: Zhenqing went to see Qi and said, "Your late father's head was delivered to Pingyuan with blood on the face; I dared not wipe it with my robe but licked it clean with my own tongue—can you bear not to make room for me!
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing went to see Qi and said, "When your father's head was brought to Pingyuan, the face was covered in blood. I would not wipe it with my robe but licked it clean with my own tongue. Can you truly refuse me a place?

sentences.zh: 杞矍然下拜，而銜恨切骨。

translations.literal: Qi started in alarm and bowed down, but harbored hatred to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Qi started in alarm and bowed low, but from that day nursed a hatred to the bone.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汝州，杞乃建遣真卿：「四方所信，若往諭之，可不勞師而定。」

translations.literal: When Li Xilie took Ru Prefecture, Qi then proposed sending Zhenqing: "He is trusted throughout the realm; if he goes to instruct Xilie, the matter may be settled without troubling the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie captured Ru Prefecture, Qi proposed sending Zhenqing: "The realm trusts him. If he goes to reason with Xilie, we may settle this without an army.

sentences.zh: 詔可，公卿皆失色。

translations.literal: The edict approved it; all the high ministers turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the plan, and the high ministers turned pale.

sentences.zh: 李勉以為失一元老，貽朝廷羞，密表固留。

translations.literal: Li Mian considered it the loss of a senior statesman and a disgrace to the court; he secretly memorialized to detain him firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian saw it as losing a senior statesman and shaming the court. He secretly memorialized to keep Zhenqing back.

sentences.zh: 至河南，河南尹鄭叔則以希烈反狀明，勸不行，答曰：「君命可避乎？」

translations.literal: When he reached Henan, Henan prefect Zheng Shuzhe, seeing Xilie's rebellion clear, urged him not to go; he answered, "Can the ruler's command be evaded?
translations.idiomatic: At Henan, prefect Zheng Shuzhe, seeing Xilie's rebellion plainly, urged him not to proceed. Zhenqing answered, "Can one evade the ruler's command?

sentences.zh: 既見希烈，宣詔旨，希烈養子千余拔刃爭進，諸將皆慢罵，將食之，真卿色不變。

translations.literal: When he met Xilie and announced the edict, Xilie's adopted sons, more than a thousand, drew blades and pressed forward; the generals all insulted and reviled him and were about to devour him; Zhenqing's expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Xilie and announced the imperial edict, more than a thousand of Xilie's adopted sons drew swords and pressed forward. The generals cursed and reviled him and were ready to tear him apart. Zhenqing's face never changed.

sentences.zh: 希烈以身捍，麾其眾退，乃就館。

translations.literal: Xilie shielded him with his own body, waved his followers back, and then lodged him in a guesthouse.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie shielded him with his own body, waved the mob back, and lodged him in a guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 逼使上疏雪己，真卿不從。

translations.literal: They pressed him to submit a memorial clearing Xilie; Zhenqing would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him to memorialize the throne in Xilie's defense. Zhenqing refused.

sentences.zh: 乃詐遣真卿兄子峴與從吏數輩繼請，德宗不報。

translations.literal: They then falsely sent Zhenqing's nephew Xian and several attendant clerks in succession to plead; Emperor Dezong did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Zhenqing's nephew Xian and several clerks in succession to plead for him. Emperor Dezong never answered.

sentences.zh: 真卿每與諸子書，但戒嚴奉家廟，恤諸孤，訖無它語。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhenqing wrote to his sons, he only admonished them to reverently maintain the ancestral temple and care for the orphans, and said nothing else to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In letters to his sons he only urged them to tend the ancestral temple and care for the orphans. He wrote of nothing else.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣李元平說之，真卿叱曰：「爾受國委任，不能致命，顧吾無兵戮汝，尚說我邪？」

translations.literal: Xilie sent Li Yuanping to persuade him; Zhenqing rebuked him, saying, "You received the state's commission yet could not give your life—yet because I have no troops to execute you, you still come to persuade me?
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent Li Yuanping to win him over. Zhenqing rebuked him: "The state entrusted you with office and you could not give your life for it. Because I have no troops to execute you, you dare come to persuade me?

sentences.zh: 希烈大會其黨，召真卿，使倡優斥侮朝廷。

translations.literal: Xilie held a great assembly of his faction, summoned Zhenqing, and had entertainers insult and humiliate the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie held a great assembly of his followers, summoned Zhenqing, and set entertainers to insult the court before him.

sentences.zh: 真卿怒曰：「公，人臣，奈何如是？」

translations.literal: Zhenqing said angrily, "Sir, you are a subject—how can you act like this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing said angrily, "You are a subject of the throne. How can you do this?

sentences.zh: 拂衣去。

translations.literal: He brushed his robe and left.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed his robe and walked out.

sentences.zh: 希烈大慚。

translations.literal: Xilie was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 時硃滔、王武俊、田悅、李納使者皆在坐，謂希烈曰：「聞太師名德久矣，公欲建大號而太師至，求宰相孰先太師者？」

translations.literal: At the time envoys of Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na were all seated; they said to Xilie, "We have long heard of the Grand Preceptor's fame and virtue; you wish to establish a great title, yet when the Grand Preceptor arrives, whom would you seek as chief minister ahead of him?
translations.idiomatic: Envoys of Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na were present. They said to Xilie, "We have long heard of the Grand Preceptor's fame. You wish to proclaim an imperial title—yet when he arrives, who would you name chief minister ahead of him?

sentences.zh: 真卿叱曰：「若等聞顏常山否？

translations.literal: Zhenqing rebuked them, saying, "Have you gentlemen heard of Yan of Changshan?
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing rebuked them: "Have you heard of Yan of Changshan?

sentences.zh: 吾兄也。

translations.literal: He was my elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: My own elder brother.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，首舉義師，後雖被執，詬賊不絕於口。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he was first to raise the loyal army; though later captured, he never ceased reviling the traitors with his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, he was first to raise loyal troops. Though later captured, he never stopped cursing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 吾年且八十，官太師，吾守吾節，死而後已，豈受若等脅邪！」

translations.literal: I am nearly eighty, hold the office of Grand Preceptor—I shall keep my integrity until death; how could I accept coercion from you!"
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly eighty and hold the rank of Grand Preceptor. I shall keep my integrity until death. Do you think I would bow to your threats?"

sentences.zh: 諸賊失色。

translations.literal: All the traitors turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel envoys turned pale.

sentences.zh: 希烈乃拘真卿，守以甲士，掘方丈坎于廷，傳將坑之，真卿見希烈曰：「死生分矣，何多為！」

translations.literal: Xilie then detained Zhenqing, guarded him with armored soldiers, dug a square pit one zhang across in the courtyard, and spread word that he would bury him alive; Zhenqing saw Xilie and said, "Life and death are already decided—why all this fuss!
translations.idiomatic: Xilie detained him under armed guard, dug a square pit in the courtyard, and spread word that he would bury him alive. Zhenqing told Xilie, "Life and death are already settled. Why all this trouble?

sentences.zh: 張伯儀敗，希烈令齎旌節首級示真卿，真卿慟哭投地。

translations.literal: When Zhang Boyi was defeated, Xilie ordered the imperial banners and tally and severed heads brought to show Zhenqing; Zhenqing wailed and threw himself to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Boyi was defeated, Xilie had the imperial banners and severed heads brought to show him. Zhenqing wailed and threw himself to the ground.

sentences.zh: 會其党周曾、康秀林等謀襲希烈，奉真卿為帥。

translations.literal: Just then his faction members Zhou Zeng, Kang Xiulin, and others plotted to strike Xilie and make Zhenqing commander.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his followers, Zhou Zeng and Kang Xiulin among them, plotted to strike Xilie and make Zhenqing their commander.

sentences.zh: 事泄，曾死，乃拘送真卿蔡州。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; Zeng died; they then detained and sent Zhenqing to Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked. Zeng was killed, and Zhenqing was sent under guard to Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真卿度必死，乃作遺表、墓誌、祭文，指寢室西壁下曰：「此吾殯所也。」

translations.literal: Zhenqing judged he would surely die; he then composed a final memorial, tomb inscription, and sacrificial text, and pointing below the west wall of his sleeping chamber said, "This is where I shall lie in my coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he would die, he wrote his final memorial, tomb inscription, and funeral text, and pointing below the west wall of his chamber said, "This is where I shall lie in my coffin.

sentences.zh: 希烈僭稱帝，使問儀式，對曰：「老夫耄矣，曾掌國禮，所記諸侯朝覲耳！」

translations.literal: When Xilie presumptuously declared himself emperor and sent someone to ask about ritual forms, he answered, "This old man is aged; I once managed the state's rites—I remember only how feudal lords attended court!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie declared himself emperor and asked about court ritual, he answered, "I am an old man. I once managed the state's rites. I remember only how feudal lords attended the Son of Heaven!"

translations.literal: Closing mark of direct speech.
translations.idiomatic: End of his reply.

sentences.zh: 興元後，王師復振，賊慮變，遣將辛景臻、安華至其所，積薪於廷曰：「不能屈節，當焚死。」

translations.literal: After Xingyuan, the imperial army revived; the traitors feared a turn of events and sent generals Xin Jingzhen and An Hua to his place; they piled firewood in the courtyard and said, "If you will not bend your integrity, you shall be burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyuan the imperial armies rallied again. Fearful of a turn in events, the rebels sent generals Xin Jingzhen and An Hua to him, piled firewood in the courtyard, and said, "If you will not submit, you shall burn.

sentences.zh: 真卿起赴火，景臻等遽止之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing rose and went toward the fire; Jingzhen and the others hastily stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing rose and walked toward the flames. Jingzhen and the others hastily stopped him.

sentences.zh: 希烈弟希倩坐硃泚誅，希烈因發怒，使閹奴等害真卿，曰：「有詔。」

translations.literal: Xilie's younger brother Xiqian was implicated in Zhu Ci's execution; Xilie thereupon flew into rage and sent eunuch slaves and others to kill Zhenqing, saying, "There is an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie's brother Xiqian was executed for ties to Zhu Ci. Xilie flew into a rage and sent eunuch attendants to kill Zhenqing, announcing, "There is an edict.

sentences.zh: 真卿再拜。

translations.literal: Zhenqing bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing performed the full obeisance.

sentences.zh: 奴曰：「宜賜卿死。」

translations.literal: The slave said, "You are fit to be granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant said, "You are granted death.

sentences.zh: 曰：「老臣無狀，罪當死，然使人何日長安來？」

translations.literal: He said, "This old minister is without merit and deserves death—but from what day did the envoy come from Chang'an?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This old minister deserves death. But when did an envoy come from Chang'an?"

sentences.zh: 奴曰：「從大樑來。」

translations.literal: The slave said, "From Daliang."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant said, "From Daliang."

sentences.zh: 罵曰：「乃逆賊耳，何詔雲！」

translations.literal: He cursed, "You are nothing but a rebel traitor—what edict is there!"
translations.idiomatic: He cursed, "You are a rebel traitor. What edict?"

sentences.zh: 遂縊殺之，年七十六。

translations.literal: They then strangled and killed him; he was seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: They strangled him. He was seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王皋聞之，泣下，三軍皆慟，因表其大節。

translations.literal: Heir Prince of Cao Li Gao heard of it, shed tears, and the whole army grieved; he thereupon memorialized his great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Gao of Cao wept when he heard the news, and the whole army mourned. He memorialized Zhenqing's supreme loyalty.

sentences.zh: 淮、蔡平，子頵、碩護喪還，帝廢朝五日，贈司徒，諡文忠，賻布帛米粟加等。

translations.literal: When Huai and Cai were pacified, his sons Yun and Shuo escorted the coffin back; the emperor suspended court for five days, posthumously appointed him Minister of Works, gave the posthumous title Cultured and Loyal, and granted funeral gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and rice at enhanced grades.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Cai were pacified, his sons Yun and Shuo escorted the coffin home. The emperor suspended court for five days, posthumously appointed him Minister of Works with the title Cultured and Loyal, and granted enhanced funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 真卿立朝正色，剛而有禮，非公言直道，不萌於心。

translations.literal: Zhenqing stood at court with stern countenance, firm yet observant of ritual; what was not public truth and the straight Way did not stir in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: At court Zhenqing stood with stern dignity, firm yet courteous. Nothing that was not public truth and the straight Way ever stirred in his heart.

sentences.zh: 天下不以姓名稱，而獨曰魯公。

translations.literal: The realm did not call him by his personal name but spoke of him only as the Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The realm did not speak his personal name but called him only the Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 如李正己、田神功、董秦、侯希逸、王玄志等，皆真卿始招起之，後皆有功。

translations.literal: Men such as Li Zhengji, Tian Shenggong, Dong Qin, Hou Xiyi, and Wang Xuanzhi were all first recruited and raised up by Zhenqing; afterward they all achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji, Tian Shenggong, Dong Qin, Hou Xiyi, Wang Xuanzhi, and others were all first recruited by Zhenqing and later won distinction.

sentences.zh: 善正、草書，筆力遒婉，世寶傳之。

translations.literal: He excelled at regular and cursive script; his brush strength was forceful and graceful; the age treasures and transmits his work.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in regular and cursive script, with a brush at once forceful and graceful. The world treasures his writing and passes it down.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，赦書授頵五品正員官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan, an amnesty edict granted Yun a regular fifth-rank appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 6 (790), an amnesty edict granted his son Yun a regular fifth-rank appointment.

sentences.zh: 開成初，又以曾孫弘式為同州參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, his great-grandson Hongshi was also made military adjutant of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era, his great-grandson Hongshi was appointed military adjutant of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：唐人柳宗元稱：「世言段太尉，大抵以為武人，一時奮不慮死以取名，非也。

translations.literal: Commentator's comment: The Tang man Liu Zongyuan said, "When the age speaks of Grand Warden Duan, it generally takes him for a military man who for a moment rushed forward without regard for death to win a name—this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Liu Zongyuan of Tang wrote, "When people speak of Grand Warden Duan, they usually take him for a soldier who once rushed heedless of death to win fame. That is wrong.

sentences.zh: 太尉為人姁姁，常低首拱手行步，言氣卑弱，未嘗以色待物；

translations.literal: The Grand Warden as a man was gentle and yielding, often walking with bowed head and clasped hands, his speech and breath humble and weak; he never met things with a harsh countenance;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Warden was gentle and unassuming, often walking with bowed head and clasped hands, speaking in a quiet, humble voice. He never met anyone with a harsh look;

sentences.zh: 人視之，儒者也。

translations.literal: those who saw him took him for a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: to all appearances he was a scholar.

sentences.zh: 遇不可，必達其志，決非偶然者。」

translations.literal: when he met what could not be tolerated, he was sure to achieve his purpose—it was assuredly no accident.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he met what could not be tolerated, he always achieved his purpose. That was no accident.

sentences.zh: 宗元不妄許人，諒其然邪，非孔子所謂仁者必有勇乎？

translations.literal: Zongyuan did not lightly praise people—can we trust that this is so? Is it not what Confucius meant in saying that the humane man must have courage?
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan did not praise people lightly. We may trust that he was right. Did not Confucius say that the humane man must have courage?

sentences.zh: 當祿山反，哮噬無前，魯公獨以烏合嬰其鋒，功雖不成，其志有足稱者。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled and roared forward devouring all before him, the Duke of Lu alone with a rabble met his sharp edge; though merit was not achieved, his resolve is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled and swept all before him, the Duke of Lu alone met his armies with a hastily gathered force. Though he did not win lasting victory, his resolve deserves lasting praise.

sentences.zh: 晚節偃蹇，為奸臣所擠，見殞賊手。

translations.literal: In his later years he was obstructed and forced down, squeezed out by treacherous ministers, and perished at traitors' hands.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was obstructed and driven out by treacherous ministers, and died at traitors' hands.

sentences.zh: 毅然之氣，折而不沮，可謂忠矣。

translations.literal: His resolute spirit was broken but not discouraged—this may be called loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: His resolute spirit was broken but never bent. That may truly be called loyalty.

sentences.zh: 詳觀二子行事，當時亦不能盡信於君，及臨大節，蹈之無貳色，何耶？

translations.literal: Examining in detail the conduct of these two men, at the time they also could not win full trust from their rulers—yet when they faced the great test of integrity, they trod it without a second thought—why?
translations.idiomatic: Look closely at these two men's careers: their rulers never fully trusted them in ordinary times. Yet when the supreme test came, they met it without hesitation. Why?

sentences.zh: 彼忠臣誼士，寧以未見信望於人，要返諸己得其正，而後慊於中而行之也。

translations.literal: Those loyal ministers and righteous scholars would rather not look to others for trust and hope, but must return to themselves and gain what is right, and only then be content within and act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers do not wait to be trusted by others. They set their own conduct right first, find peace within, and then act.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，雖千五百歲，其英烈言言，如嚴霜烈日，可畏而仰哉！

translations.literal: Alas, though fifteen hundred years have passed, their heroic brightness still speaks clearly, like severe frost and blazing sun—awesome and worthy of reverence!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! Though fifteen hundred years have passed, their heroic brightness still speaks as clearly as severe frost and blazing sun—awesome and worthy of reverence!
